55# --- UX-9: sliders you can also type an exact value into ---------------------- 

56# A slider is the right control for "sweep until it looks right", but it can't be 

57# set to a precise value — awkward when a figure has to match a spec (marker size 

58# 12, opacity 0.65, line width 1.5). These wrappers pair each slider with a 

59# number box. 

60# 

61# The SLIDER keeps the canonical session key, so nothing downstream changes: deep 

62# links, Share, Save & restore and `_collect_viz_settings` all still read 

63# `global_*` / `cmp*_*` / `single_*` exactly as before. The box owns a shadow 

64# `{key}__num*` key and writes the canonical one from its `on_change`; the 

65# canonical value is mirrored back into the box *before* either widget renders, 

66# so a slider drag, a deep link, a restored config and a Quick-view preset all 

67# move the box too — one-way sync each direction, no feedback loop. 

68 

69 

70def _shadow_key_missing(*keys: str) -> bool: 

71 """True when a number box's shadow key is not in session state (BUG-18). 

72 

73 An ``on_change`` callback runs *before* the script that would (re)create the 

74 widget, and Streamlit drops a widget's key at the end of any run in which it 

75 did not render. Several of these boxes are conditional — the heatmap 

76 colour-range pair only renders when the current trial/metric has data — so a 

77 change queued while a slow rerun was still in flight can reach a callback 

78 whose own key no longer exists, and reading it raised ``KeyError`` and took 

79 the app down mid-rerun. 

80 

81 A missing shadow key means there is no user edit left to apply: the canonical 

82 key still holds the last committed value, and the box re-seeds from it the 

83 next time it renders. So the callback becomes a no-op rather than a crash. 

84 """ 

85 return any(k not in st.session_state for k in keys) 

86

88def _numeric_slider( 

89 host, 

90 label: str, 

91 *, 

92 key: str, 

93 min_value, 

94 max_value, 

95 step=None, 

96 slider_format: Optional[str] = None, 

97 number_format: Optional[str] = None, 

98 help: Optional[str] = None, 

99 disabled: bool = False, 

100 on_change=None, 

101 persist_state: Optional[str] = None, 

102) -> None: 

103 """A single-value slider plus a number box bound to the same setting. 

104 

105 ``number_format`` defaults to ``slider_format``; pass it separately when the 

106 slider's format carries a unit suffix (``"%.1f px"``), which ``number_input`` 

107 does not accept. 

108 

109 ``disabled`` greys BOTH halves (VIZ-21) without touching the canonical key — 

110 a disabled Streamlit widget still owns and keeps its value, so a mode toggle 

111 never rewrites a deep-linked / restored setting. 

112 """ 

113 num_key = f"{key}__num" 

114 if key in st.session_state: 

115 st.session_state[num_key] = st.session_state[key] 

116 

117 def _apply() -> None: 

118 if _shadow_key_missing(num_key): # BUG-18 

119 return 

120 st.session_state[key] = st.session_state[num_key] 

121 if on_change is not None: 

122 on_change() 

123 

124 # A narrow box on the same line as the slider: the box is for typing an 

125 # exact value, so it only needs room for the number itself (the CSS drops its 

126 # +/- steppers and caps its width), and the slider keeps most of the row. 

127 slider_col, num_col = host.columns([5, 1.5], vertical_alignment="bottom") 

128 slider_col.slider( 

129 label, 

130 min_value=min_value, 

131 max_value=max_value, 

132 step=step, 

133 format=slider_format, 

134 key=key, 

135 help=help, 

136 disabled=disabled, 

137 on_change=on_change, 

138 persist_state=persist_state, 

139 ) 

140 num_col.number_input( 

141 label, 

142 min_value=min_value, 

143 max_value=max_value, 

144 step=step, 

145 format=number_format if number_format is not None else slider_format, 

146 key=num_key, 

147 on_change=_apply, 

148 label_visibility="collapsed", 

149 disabled=disabled, 

150 ) 

151

153def _range_slider( 

154 host, 

155 label: str, 

156 *, 

157 key: str, 

158 min_value, 

159 max_value, 

160 step=None, 

161 slider_format: Optional[str] = None, 

162 number_format: Optional[str] = None, 

163 help: Optional[str] = None, 

164 disabled: bool = False, 

165 on_change=None, 

166 persist_state: Optional[str] = None, 

167) -> None: 

168 """A two-handle range slider plus min/max number boxes, all on one line. 

169 

170 The boxes are deliberately small — they hold a number, not a sentence — so 

171 the slider still gets most of the row. A min typed above the max is swapped 

172 rather than rejected. ``disabled`` greys all three without changing the 

173 stored range (VIZ-21). 

174 """ 

175 lo_key, hi_key = f"{key}__num_lo", f"{key}__num_hi" 

176 current = st.session_state.get(key) 

177 if isinstance(current, (tuple, list)) and len(current) == 2: 

178 st.session_state[lo_key], st.session_state[hi_key] = current 

179 

180 def _apply() -> None: 

181 if _shadow_key_missing(lo_key, hi_key): # BUG-18 

182 return 

183 lo, hi = st.session_state[lo_key], st.session_state[hi_key] 

184 st.session_state[key] = (min(lo, hi), max(lo, hi)) 

185 if on_change is not None: 

186 on_change() 

187 

188 slider_col, lo_col, hi_col = host.columns( 

189 [5, 1.5, 1.5], vertical_alignment="bottom" 

190 ) 

191 slider_col.slider( 

192 label, 

193 min_value=min_value, 

194 max_value=max_value, 

195 step=step, 

196 format=slider_format, 

197 key=key, 

198 help=help, 

199 disabled=disabled, 

200 on_change=on_change, 

201 persist_state=persist_state, 

202 ) 

203 fmt = number_format if number_format is not None else slider_format 

204 for col, num_key, side in ((lo_col, lo_key, "min"), (hi_col, hi_key, "max")): 

205 col.number_input( 

206 f"{label} ({side})", 

207 min_value=min_value, 

208 max_value=max_value, 

209 step=step, 

210 format=fmt, 

211 key=num_key, 

212 on_change=_apply, 

213 label_visibility="collapsed", 

214 disabled=disabled, 

215 )

218# VIZ-4: MIME by extension for a user-uploaded stimulus image → a `data:` URI the 

219# figure builders accept as `background_image` (plots._image_to_data_uri passes a 

220# `data:` URI straight through). 

221_UPLOAD_IMAGE_MIME = { 

222 "png": "image/png", 

223 "jpg": "image/jpeg", 

224 "jpeg": "image/jpeg", 

225 "gif": "image/gif", 

226 "webp": "image/webp", 

227} 

228 

229 

230def _uploaded_image_data_uri(uploaded) -> Optional[str]: 

231 """Base64 ``data:`` URI for a Streamlit ``UploadedFile`` image, or ``None``. 

232 

233 Cached in session state keyed by the file's id so a multi-MB screenshot is 

234 encoded once, not on every rerun (VIZ-4).""" 

235 if uploaded is None: 

236 return None 

237 import base64 

238 

239 cache = st.session_state.get("_stimulus_image_upload_cache") 

240 if isinstance(cache, dict) and cache.get("id") == uploaded.file_id: 

241 return cache.get("uri") 

242 ext = (uploaded.name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] if "." in uploaded.name else "").lower() 

243 mime = _UPLOAD_IMAGE_MIME.get(ext, "image/png") 

244 uri = f"data:{mime};base64," + base64.b64encode(uploaded.getvalue()).decode("ascii") 

245 st.session_state["_stimulus_image_upload_cache"] = { 

246 "id": uploaded.file_id, 

247 "uri": uri, 

248 } 

249 return uri

256# --- VIZ-21/23: which rail controls actually apply in Animate / Compare ------- 

257# One rail feeds the static, animation, and comparison renderers, but some layers 

258# do not exist in every mode. Each affected control therefore declares which 

259# render paths consume it. Unsupported controls stay visible but disabled so the 

260# reason is discoverable, and their stored values survive mode switches, deep 

261# links, and restored configs. Keep the authoritative setting → render-path 

262# table in `CLAUDE.md` in sync with these gates. 

263 

264 

265def _mode_gate( 

266 animating: bool, 

267 comparing: bool, 

268 *, 

269 in_animation: bool = True, 

270 in_compare: bool = True, 

271) -> tuple[bool, str]: 

272 """``(disabled, reason)`` for a control, given which paths honour it. 

273 

274 ``in_animation`` / ``in_compare`` state whether the corresponding builder 

275 actually consumes the setting. The reason string is prefixed onto the 

276 control's ``help`` so the tooltip explains the greying instead of leaving 

277 the user guessing.""" 

278 modes = [] 

279 if animating and not in_animation: 

280 modes.append("**Animate**") 

281 if comparing and not in_compare: 

282 modes.append("**Compare**") 

283 if not modes: 

284 return False, "" 

285 return True, ( 

286 "⚠️ Not available in " + " / ".join(modes) + " mode — that render path " 

287 "ignores this setting. Your value is kept and applies again once the " 

288 "mode is off." 

289 ) 

290 

291 

292def _gated_help(base: Optional[str], reason: str) -> Optional[str]: 

293 """Prefix ``reason`` (from :func:`_mode_gate`) onto a control's help text.""" 

294 if not reason: 

295 return base 

296 return f"{reason}\n\n{base}" if base else reason

483def _render_fixclass_category( 

484 key_prefix: str, 

485 label: str, 

486 *, 

487 threshold_label: Optional[str] = None, 

488 disabled: bool = False, 

489 reason: str = "", 

490) -> None: 

491 """Render one fixation-classification category (PRE-2) inside the Fixation popover. 

492 

493 A mode radio (Off / Highlight / Discard); when not Off and ``threshold_label`` 

494 is given, a ms threshold number input; when Highlight, a marker + colour picker. 

495 All values ride ``global_fixclass_{key_prefix}_*`` keys (seeded in 

496 ``_VIZ_WIDGET_DEFAULTS``). ``disabled``/``reason`` come from 

497 :func:`_mode_gate` — since VIZ-23 the flags reach the static figure *and* the 

498 animated replay, but no comparison builder takes them.""" 

499 mode = st.radio( 

500 label, 

501 options=_FIXCLASS_MODES, 

502 horizontal=True, 

503 key=f"global_fixclass_{key_prefix}_mode", 

504 persist_state="session", 

505 help=_gated_help( 

506 "Highlight marks these fixations with an overlay marker; Discard hides " 

507 "them from the plot only (reading measures and exported tables are " 

508 "unchanged).", 

509 reason, 

510 ), 

511 disabled=disabled, 

512 ) 

513 if threshold_label is not None and mode != "Off": 

514 st.number_input( 

515 threshold_label, 

516 min_value=1, 

517 step=10, 

518 key=f"global_fixclass_{key_prefix}_threshold_ms", 

519 persist_state="session", 

520 disabled=disabled, 

521 ) 

522 if mode == "Highlight": 

523 st.selectbox( 

524 "Marker", 

525 options=list(_OUT_OF_TEXT_MARKERS), 

526 format_func=lambda s: _OUT_OF_TEXT_MARKERS[s], 

527 key=f"global_fixclass_{key_prefix}_symbol", 

528 persist_state="session", 

529 disabled=disabled, 

530 ) 

531 st.color_picker( 

532 "Color", key=f"global_fixclass_{key_prefix}_color", disabled=disabled 

533 )

536def _render_fixation_cleaning(*, disabled: bool = False, reason: str = "") -> None: 

537 """PRE-2 short / long / out-of-bounds visual filtering controls. 

538 

539 VIZ-27 gives this its own popover instead of burying data inclusion under 

540 marker styling. Viz-only: highlight or discard, with 

541 customizable short/long thresholds, all on the spot. 

542 

543 ``make_scanpath_figure`` and ``make_scanpath_animation`` both consume 

544 ``fixation_flags`` (VIZ-23 — *Discard* drops the rows before the replay's 

545 frames are built, *Highlight* overlays them as the trail reaches them); the 

546 comparison builders take no flags argument, so the whole block renders 

547 disabled (with the reason) in Compare only.""" 

548 st.caption("Highlight or hide classes on the plot only") 

549 for prefix, label, threshold in ( 

550 ("short", "Short fixations", "Short threshold (ms)"), 

551 ("long", "Long fixations", "Long threshold (ms)"), 

552 ("oob", "Out-of-bounds fixations", None), 

553 ("blink", "Blink / blink-adjacent fixations", None), 

554 ): 

555 _render_fixclass_category( 

556 prefix, 

557 label, 

558 threshold_label=threshold, 

559 disabled=disabled, 

560 reason=reason, 

561 ) 

562

566 ``global_fixclass_*`` session keys (PRE-2). One entry per category; ``oob`` has 

567 no threshold.""" 

568 ss = st.session_state 

569 return { 

570 "short": {

579 "symbol": ss.get("global_fixclass_long_symbol") or "square-open", 

580 "color": ss.get("global_fixclass_long_color") or "#9467bd", 

581 },

595def _fixation_filter_badge() -> str: 

596 """Compact VIZ-27 badge summarising active visual filters.""" 

597 active = [ 

598 st.session_state.get(f"global_fixclass_{name}_mode", "Off") 

599 for name in ("short", "long", "oob", "blink") 

600 ] 

601 n_active = sum(mode != "Off" for mode in active) 

602 n_discard = sum(mode == "Discard" for mode in active) 

603 if not n_active: 

604 return "" 

605 detail = f"{n_active} active" 

606 if n_discard: 

607 detail += f", {n_discard} hidden" 

608 return f" · {detail}" 

609 

610 

611def _saccade_filter_badge() -> str: 

612 """Compact badge summarising the VIZ-31 saccade reading-class filter. 

613 

614 Mirrors :func:`_fixation_filter_badge` — an active filter must be visible 

615 without opening the popover, or a figure missing half its saccades reads as 

616 a data problem. Empty (or a full selection) means no filter, so no badge. 

617 """ 

618 selected = st.session_state.get("global_saccade_classes") 

619 if not selected: 

620 return "" 

621 hidden = [cls for cls in SACCADE_CLASS_ORDER if cls not in set(selected)] 

622 if not hidden: 

623 return "" 

624 if len(hidden) == len(SACCADE_CLASS_ORDER) - 1: 

625 # One class left standing — name it; "5 hidden" says much less than 

626 # "regression only" when that is the whole point of the figure. 

627 kept = next(c for c in SACCADE_CLASS_ORDER if c not in set(hidden)) 

628 return f" · {SACCADE_CLASS_LABELS[kept].lower()} only" 

629 return f" · {len(hidden)} hidden"

632# Quick-view presets: one click sets the *layer* toggles to a focused subset, so 

633# a user lands on a legible picture instead of toggling layers one by one. The 

634# Illustration preset also applies four presentation overrides. Those overrides 

635# are temporary: ``_apply_view_preset`` snapshots them on the way in and restores 

636# them on the way out, so Illustration → Scanpath cannot leave arc/snap/opacity 

637# settings behind while the button says Scanpath. Other per-layer styling 

638# (colours, sizes, colorscales) remains untouched. 

639_ILLUSTRATION_OVERRIDE_KEYS = ( 

640 "global_saccade_render_mode", 

641 "global_fixation_snap_to_word", 

642 "global_saccade_color_mode", 

643 "global_fixation_opacity",

645_PRE_ILLUSTRATION_STATE = "_quick_view_pre_illustration"

704def _apply_view_preset(name: str) -> None: 

705 """Apply a Quick-view preset and keep Illustration overrides reversible. 

706 

707 Runs as a button ``on_click`` callback, i.e. *before* the next rerun 

708 instantiates the layer checkboxes — so writing their ``global_show_*`` keys 

709 here is picked up cleanly (no "set after widget instantiated" warning). 

710 

711 Illustration owns four style/geometry values that ordinary quick views do 

712 not. Preserve their incoming values once, then restore each value that is 

713 still carrying Illustration's override when another preset is selected. A 

714 value edited explicitly while Illustration is active is therefore retained. 

715 """ 

716 if name not in _VIEW_PRESETS: 

717 raise ValueError(f"Unknown quick-view preset: {name}") 

718 

719 ss = st.session_state 

720 illustration = _VIEW_PRESETS["illustration"] 

721 was_illustration = all(ss.get(key) == value for key, value in illustration.items()) 

722 if name == "illustration": 

723 if _PRE_ILLUSTRATION_STATE not in ss: 

724 ss[_PRE_ILLUSTRATION_STATE] = { 

725 key: ( 

726 _VIZ_WIDGET_DEFAULTS[key] 

727 if was_illustration 

728 else ss.get(key, _VIZ_WIDGET_DEFAULTS[key]) 

729 ) 

730 for key in _ILLUSTRATION_OVERRIDE_KEYS 

731 } 

732 else: 

733 previous = ss.pop(_PRE_ILLUSTRATION_STATE, None) 

734 # A saved config, deep link, or hot-reloaded session can enter on the 

735 # Illustration values without ever running the callback that captures a 

736 # snapshot. Falling back to the ordinary defaults still makes the exit 

737 # deterministic instead of leaving Illustration geometry behind. 

738 if previous is None and was_illustration: 

739 previous = { 

740 key: _VIZ_WIDGET_DEFAULTS[key] for key in _ILLUSTRATION_OVERRIDE_KEYS 

741 } 

742 if previous is not None: 

743 for key in _ILLUSTRATION_OVERRIDE_KEYS: 

744 # Do not overwrite an explicit edit made after Illustration was 

745 # applied; only undo the value the preset itself still owns. 

746 if ss.get(key) == illustration[key]: 

747 ss[key] = previous.get(key, _VIZ_WIDGET_DEFAULTS[key]) 

748 

749 for key, value in _VIEW_PRESETS[name].items(): 

750 ss[key] = value 

751 

752 

753def _active_quick_view() -> Optional[str]: 

754 """Return the quick-view preset whose owned values match current state. 

755 

756 Illustration is deliberately checked before Scanpath: its layer set is a 

757 superset of the Scanpath contract, so the old order mislabeled an active 

758 Illustration as Scanpath even while arc-and-snap geometry remained live. 

759 """ 

760 ss = st.session_state 

761 for name in ("illustration", "scanpath", "heatmap"): 

762 if all(ss.get(k) == v for k, v in _VIEW_PRESETS[name].items()): 

763 return name 

764 return None 

765 

766 

767# VIZ-18: palette setting name → the session key it writes. A palette is applied 

768# by writing the *ordinary* colour keys, so nothing downstream has to know 

769# palettes exist — the per-element pickers, the deep link, Save & restore, the 

770# CLI and the API all keep carrying plain colours. 

771_PALETTE_STATE_KEYS = { 

772 "fixation_color": "global_fixation_color", 

773 "fixation_colorscale": "global_fixation_colorscale", 

774 "heatmap_colorscale": "global_heatmap_colorscale", 

775 "saccade_color": "global_saccade_color", 

776 "word_label_color": "global_text_color", 

777 "highlight_text_color": "global_highlight_text_color", 

778} 

779 

780 

781def palette_state(name: str) -> Dict: 

782 """The ``session_state`` writes that applying palette ``name`` performs.""" 

783 settings = palette_settings(name) 

784 state = { 

785 state_key: settings[setting] 

786 for setting, state_key in _PALETTE_STATE_KEYS.items() 

787 if setting in settings 

788 } 

789 for cls_name, color in settings.get("saccade_class_colors", {}).items(): 

790 if cls_name in SACCADE_CLASS_EDITABLE: 

791 state[f"global_saccade_class_color_{cls_name}"] = color 

792 return state 

793 

794 

795def apply_palette(name: str) -> None: 

796 """Apply a VIZ-18 palette by writing its colours into ``session_state``. 

797 

798 Runs as a widget ``on_change`` callback — i.e. before the next rerun 

799 instantiates the colour pickers — so writing their keys here is picked up 

800 cleanly, exactly like ``_apply_view_preset``. Deliberately does *not* touch 

801 the background colour: that's a canvas/Experimental-Setup choice the user 

802 makes for their output medium, not part of the mark palette. 

803 

804 ``CUSTOM_PALETTE`` is a no-op: it names the *absence* of a palette, so 

805 re-selecting it must not overwrite the colours the user just set by hand. 

806 """ 

807 if name == CUSTOM_PALETTE: 

808 return 

809 for key, value in palette_state(name).items(): 

810 st.session_state[key] = value 

811 

812 

813def _palette_match_key(value): 

814 """Normalize a colour for comparison — the pickers hand back lowercase hex.""" 

815 return value.lower() if isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith("#") else value 

816 

817 

818def _active_palette() -> Optional[str]: 

819 """Which palette the live colour keys match, or ``None`` once customized. 

820 

821 The VIZ-12 rule applied to VIZ-18: a palette is one-way (it writes the 

822 ordinary colour keys and never reads them back), so without this the selector 

823 keeps reading "Colourblind-safe" after the user has hand-edited one of its 

824 colours — naming a property the figure no longer has. 

825 """ 

826 ss = st.session_state 

827 for name in PALETTES: 

828 wanted = palette_state(name) 

829 if all( 

830 _palette_match_key(ss.get(key)) == _palette_match_key(value) 

831 for key, value in wanted.items() 

832 ): 

833 return name 

834 return None 

835 

836 

837def _on_palette_change() -> None: 

838 name = st.session_state.get("global_palette") or DEFAULT_PALETTE 

839 if name != CUSTOM_PALETTE: 

840 # What "Custom" is a departure *from*, for the caption below. 

841 st.session_state["_palette_picked"] = name 

842 apply_palette(name) 

843

845def _popover_selectbox(label: str, options: list, state_key: str, **kwargs): 

846 """A selectbox inside a popover whose seeded session value actually shows. 

847 

848 A *keyed* selectbox first painted inside a (closed-until-clicked) popover 

849 renders its first option rather than the value seeded into session state, and 

850 commits that wrong value on the next interaction — the same first-open quirk 

851 the VIZ-8 class colour pickers hit. Passing an explicit ``index=`` and writing 

852 the pick back by hand sidesteps it, which is what lets a VIZ-18 palette (or a 

853 deep link, or a restored config) set a non-first colorscale and have the 

854 picker agree with the figure. 

855 """ 

856 current = st.session_state.get(state_key) 

857 index = options.index(current) if current in options else 0 

858 picked = st.selectbox(label, options=options, index=index, **kwargs) 

859 st.session_state[state_key] = picked 

860 return picked

894def _default_box_format(proposed: Dict[str, Optional[str]]) -> str: 

895 """Which box encoding to show first, from what auto-detect found. 

896 

897 Edges if all four edge columns were detected, else origin+size if those four 

898 were, else edges.""" 

899 if all(proposed.get(k) for k in ("left", "right", "top", "bottom")): 

900 return BOX_FORMAT_EDGES 

901 if all(proposed.get(k) for k in ("x", "y", "width", "height")): 

902 return BOX_FORMAT_ORIGIN 

903 return BOX_FORMAT_EDGES

1132 "help": "Sample time (ms); orders the continuous gaze path. " 

1133 "Defaults to row order.", 

1134 }, 

1135 { 

1136 "key": "text", 

1137 "label": "Word text/label", 

1138 "required": False, 

1139 "help": "Optional word/label associated with the sample.", 

1140 }, 

1141] 

1142 

1143 

1144def column_mapping_ui( 

1145 df: pd.DataFrame, 

1146 table_label: str, 

1147 state_key_prefix: str, 

1148 field_specs: List[Dict], 

1149 proposed: Dict[str, Optional[str]], 

1150 expand_on_problem: bool = True, 

1151 problems: Optional[List[str]] = None, 

1152 container=None, 

1153 use_expander: bool = True, 

1154 only_keys: Optional[List[str]] = None, 

1155 header: bool = True, 

1156 detected_label: str = "auto-detected", 

1157) -> Dict[str, Optional[str]]: 

1158 """Render a column-mapping expander letting users override the inferred mapping. 

1159 

1160 Renders in the sidebar by default; pass ``container`` (e.g. a main-area 

1161 container from the setup wizard) to render it there instead. 

1162 

1163 Returns a mapping {field_key: column_name_or_None}. Fields marked 

1164 ``multi: True`` (Trial ID) render as a multiselect: picking several columns 

1165 yields a list, meaning "build this ID on the fly by joining the columns' 

1166 values" (see ``data.trial_id_series``); a single pick stays a plain string. 

1167 A field marked ``kind: "box"`` (the word box) renders a coordinate-format 

1168 radio plus the four sub-fields for that format, and expands into all eight 

1169 box keys (the four inactive ones set to None) so the returned schema keeps 

1170 its fixed shape. 

1171 """ 

1172 options = [NONE_OPTION] + list(df.columns) 

1173 expanded = bool(expand_on_problem and problems) 

1174 

1175 def _selectbox(field_key: str, field_label: str, help_text=None) -> Optional[str]: 

1176 default = proposed.get(field_key) 

1177 index = options.index(default) if default in options else 0 

1178 chosen = st.selectbox( 

1179 field_label, 

1180 options=options, 

1181 index=index, 

1182 key=f"{state_key_prefix}_{field_key}", 

1183 help=help_text, 

1184 ) 

1185 # Surface what auto-detection found for this field (ENG-9) — and flag when 

1186 # the user has overridden it — so the mapping isn't silently inferred. 

1187 if default and default in df.columns: 

1188 if chosen != default and chosen != NONE_OPTION: 

1189 st.caption(f"✨ {detected_label} `{default}` · overridden") 

1190 else: 

1191 st.caption(f"✨ {detected_label} `{default}`") 

1192 return None if chosen == NONE_OPTION else chosen 

1193 

1194 host = container if container is not None else st.sidebar 

1195 # Render inside an expander by default; ``use_expander=False`` renders inline 

1196 # (the collapsed wizard panel already lives in an expander — Streamlit forbids 

1197 # nesting expanders). 

1198 section = ( 

1199 host.expander(f"Column mapping — {table_label}", expanded=expanded) 

1200 if use_expander 

1201 else host.container() 

1202 ) 

1203 with section: 

1204 if not use_expander and header: 

1205 st.markdown(f"**Column mapping — {table_label}**") 

1206 if header: 

1207 st.caption( 

1208 "Auto-detected from your CSV. Override any row if your column " 

1209 "names differ." 

1210 ) 

1211 if problems: 

1212 st.warning( 

1213 "Fix these before the app can use this table: " + "; ".join(problems) 

1214 ) 

1215 mapping: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {} 

1216 for spec in field_specs: 

1217 key = spec["key"] 

1218 # When ``only_keys`` is given, render just that subset (the wizard 

1219 # renders fields in grouped, ordered steps). 

1220 if only_keys is not None and key not in only_keys: 

1221 continue 

1222 default = proposed.get(key) 

1223 label = spec["label"] + (" *" if spec.get("required") else "") 

1224 if spec.get("kind") == "box": 

1225 fmt_key = f"{state_key_prefix}_box_format" 

1226 if fmt_key not in st.session_state: 

1227 # Seed via session state (no `index=`) so it survives reruns 

1228 # and never fights a default arg — same pattern as the 

1229 # multiselect below. 

1230 st.session_state[fmt_key] = _default_box_format(proposed) 

1231 star = " \\*" if spec.get("required") else "" 

1232 st.markdown(f"**{spec['label']}**{star}") 

1233 if spec.get("help"): 

1234 st.caption(spec["help"]) 

1235 fmt = st.radio( 

1236 "Coordinate format", 

1237 options=list(_BOX_SUBFIELDS), 

1238 key=fmt_key, 

1239 horizontal=True, 

1240 label_visibility="collapsed", 

1241 ) 

1242 # Always emit all eight box keys; only the active format's four 

1243 # get a column, the rest stay None. 

1244 mapping.update({box_key: None for box_key in _ALL_BOX_KEYS}) 

1245 for sub_key, sub_label in _BOX_SUBFIELDS[fmt]: 

1246 mapping[sub_key] = _selectbox(sub_key, sub_label) 

1247 continue 

1248 if spec.get("multi"): 

1249 state_key = f"{state_key_prefix}_{key}" 

1250 proposed_default = [default] if default in df.columns else [] 

1251 stored = st.session_state.get(state_key) 

1252 if stored is None: 

1253 # Seed via session state instead of `default=` so the 

1254 # stale-column reset below never fights a default arg. 

1255 st.session_state[state_key] = proposed_default 

1256 else: 

1257 # A new upload changes the column universe — silently 

1258 # keeping stale picks would leave the field empty (the 

1259 # selectboxes self-heal via their index fallback; a 

1260 # multiselect doesn't). Drop unknown columns and fall 

1261 # back to the auto-proposal when nothing survives. 

1262 valid = [c for c in stored if c in df.columns] 

1263 if len(valid) != len(stored): 

1264 st.session_state[state_key] = valid or proposed_default 

1265 chosen_cols = st.multiselect( 

1266 label, 

1267 options=list(df.columns), 

1268 key=state_key, 

1269 help=spec.get("help"), 

1270 ) 

1271 if default and default in df.columns: 

1272 st.caption(f"✨ {detected_label} `{default}`") 

1273 if not chosen_cols: 

1274 mapping[key] = None 

1275 elif len(chosen_cols) == 1: 

1276 mapping[key] = chosen_cols[0] 

1277 else: 

1278 mapping[key] = list(chosen_cols) 

1279 continue 

1280 mapping[key] = _selectbox(key, label, spec.get("help")) 

1281 return mapping 

1282 

1283

1324def color_field_options(trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame) -> List[str]: 

1325 """Columns offered in the 'Color fixations by' selector — a preferred order 

1326 intersected with what's present, falling back to ``['duration_ms']``.""" 

1327 preferred_color_fields = [ 

1328 "duration_ms", 

1329 "pass_index", 

1330 "eye", 

1331 "saccade_type", 

1332 "saccade_amplitude",

1340 "universal_pos", 

1341 "ptb_pos", 

1342 ] 

1343 fields = [f for f in preferred_color_fields if f in trial_fixations.columns]

1345 # `(uniform)` leads and is the default (VIZ-17): marker *size* already encodes

1349 # fixation by the text line it lands on, inferred from word geometry.

1421def _drop_stale(state_key: str, options: list) -> None: 

1422 """Clear a persisted selectbox value that isn't valid for the current 

1423 ``options`` (e.g. after switching datasets, or restoring a config built on 

1424 different data) so ``st.selectbox`` falls back to its ``index=`` default 

1425 instead of raising. Mirrors the guard in ``utils._select_trial_composite_mode``.""" 

1426 if state_key in st.session_state and st.session_state[state_key] not in options: 

1427 del st.session_state[state_key] 

1428 

1429 

1430def _drop_stale_multi(state_key: str, options: list) -> None: 

1431 """Keep only still-valid values in a persisted multiselect list.""" 

1432 value = st.session_state.get(state_key) 

1433 if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)): 

1434 filtered = [item for item in value if item in options] 

1435 if list(value) != filtered: 

1436 st.session_state[state_key] = filtered 

1437 elif value is not None: 

1438 st.session_state.pop(state_key, None) 

1439 

1440 

1441def _clamp_range(state_key: str, lo: float, hi: float) -> None: 

1442 """Clamp a persisted ``(min, max)`` range-slider value into ``[lo, hi]`` so a 

1443 restored value built on different data can't fall outside the slider bounds 

1444 and raise. Drops anything that isn't a 2-tuple.""" 

1445 val = st.session_state.get(state_key) 

1446 if not (isinstance(val, (list, tuple)) and len(val) == 2): 

1447 st.session_state.pop(state_key, None) 

1448 return 

1449 try: 

1450 a, b = float(val[0]), float(val[1]) 

1451 except (TypeError, ValueError): 

1452 del st.session_state[state_key] 

1453 return 

1454 a, b = max(lo, min(a, hi)), max(lo, min(b, hi)) 

1455 st.session_state[state_key] = (min(a, b), max(a, b)) 

1456 

1457 

1458def _clamped_pair(val, lo: float, hi: float) -> Optional[tuple]: 

1459 """Pure twin of ``_clamp_range``: clamp a stored ``(min, max)`` into ``[lo, 

1460 hi]`` and return it, or ``None`` for a malformed/missing value — WITHOUT 

1461 touching session_state. Used by ``_collect_viz_settings`` (the non-rendering 

1462 reader) so a colour range stored on differently-scaled data is clamped the 

1463 same way the rendered slider clamps it, instead of leaking out-of-bounds into 

1464 the Corpus / Save-&-restore figures.""" 

1465 if not (isinstance(val, (list, tuple)) and len(val) == 2): 

1466 return None 

1467 try: 

1468 a, b = float(val[0]), float(val[1]) 

1469 except (TypeError, ValueError): 

1470 return None 

1471 a, b = max(lo, min(a, hi)), max(lo, min(b, hi)) 

1472 return (min(a, b), max(a, b)) 

1473 

1474

1478def render_pattern_help(host, fields: dict) -> None: 

1479 """The one place the ``{field}`` vocabulary is spelled out (UX-31). 

1480 

1481 Three surfaces speak this little language — the figure title/caption, the 

1482 Compare A/B legend labels, and the bulk-export file-naming pattern — and two 

1483 of them used to describe it only as "same fields as the other one", so a user 

1484 who had seen neither had no way to learn that ``{participant_id}`` was even a 

1485 thing. Rendered as a collapsed expander: it is reference material, not a 

1486 control, and the rail is narrow. 

1487 """ 

1488 if not fields: 

1489 return 

1490 with host.expander("Available fields", expanded=False): 

1491 st.markdown( 

1492 "Type any of these in a pattern and the trial's own value is " 

1493 "substituted:\n\n" 

1494 + "\n".join(f"- `{{{name}}}`" for name in sorted(fields)) 

1495 + "\n\nAnything else is left as literal text." 

1496 ) 

1497 

1498 

1499def render_pattern_input( 

1500 host, 

1501 label: str, 

1502 key: str, 

1503 fields: dict, 

1504 *, 

1505 help: Optional[str] = None, 

1506 placeholder: Optional[str] = None, 

1507) -> str: 

1508 """A pattern text box with live validation and a rendered preview. 

1509 

1510 Returns the pattern, or ``""`` when it names a field that does not exist — 

1511 an invalid pattern must not reach a figure or a filename, and the error says 

1512 which placeholder is wrong (see ``export.pattern_error``). 

1513 

1514 ``placeholder`` is what an *empty* box falls back to, printed greyed inside 

1515 the box itself (UX-31). These boxes default to empty — the fallback used to 

1516 be stated only in the `help` tooltip, so the one thing you need to know 

1517 before typing (what you get if you don't) needed a hover to find. 

1518 

1519 Pass it **only** where an empty box really does produce that string. The 

1520 Compare A/B labels qualify (empty → the auto ``participant · trial``); the 

1521 figure title/caption do not (empty → no title at all), and a placeholder 

1522 there would promise the opposite of what happens. 

1523 """ 

1524 host.text_input( 

1525 label, key=key, persist_state="session", help=help, placeholder=placeholder 

1526 ) 

1527 value = st.session_state.get(key, "") 

1528 if not value: 

1529 return "" 

1530 error = pattern_error(value, fields) 

1531 if error: 

1532 host.error(error) 

1533 return "" 

1534 host.caption(f"{label} preview — **{render_pattern(value, fields)}**") 

1535 return value 

1536 

1537 

1538def _pin(key: str, default) -> None: 

1539 """Seed ``key``'s default if it has none yet. Never overwrites. 

1540 

1541 This is the *first value* half of the widget-state contract. The other half 

1542 — keeping that value alive through runs where the widget doesn't render, and 

1543 pushing it to the browser when the widget finally mounts — used to be a 

1544 matching ``rewrite=True`` re-assertion here (BUG-15: Streamlit only sent a 

1545 value down on the run it was written programmatically, so a control whose 

1546 popover first opened on a *later* run mounted at its proto default — nothing 

1547 pressed on a segmented control, black on a colour picker). Streamlit 1.61 

1548 owns that natively: every widget on these keys passes 

1549 ``persist_state="session"``, which preserves the value while unmounted and 

1550 marks it as changed on remount so the frontend adopts it (ENG-36). Keep the 

1551 kwarg when adding a widget on a ``global_*`` / ``single_*`` / ``cmp{idx}_*`` 

1552 key — it is what makes this a plain ``setdefault`` again. 

1553 

1554 Safe only because no viz widget passes ``value=``/``index=`` (see 

1555 ``_seed_viz_state``); adding one would fight the stored value *and* log 

1556 Streamlit's "default value but also set via Session State API" warning. 

1557 

1558 A **list** default is copied on the way in: ``_VIZ_WIDGET_DEFAULTS`` is a 

1559 module-level table, so seeding a multiselect (``global_saccade_classes``) 

1560 with the list object itself would hand session state a live alias of the 

1561 default, and one in-place edit anywhere would change it for the rest of the 

1562 process. 

1563 """ 

1564 if key in st.session_state: 

1565 return 

1566 try: 

1567 st.session_state[key] = list(default) if isinstance(default, list) else default 

1568 except StreamlitAPIException: 

1569 # The key belongs to a widget already created this run (⚙ Compare 

1570 # options / ⚙ Playback render in tabs.py before the rail). It is already 

1571 # carrying its value, so there is nothing to seed. 

1572 pass 

1573 

1574 

1575def _seed_compare_styles() -> None: 

1576 """Seed the per-scanpath comparison styling keys (so the collected dicts have 

1577 values even when the relevant layer popover isn't open this run). 

1578 

1579 Seeding is all that is needed: the widgets themselves carry 

1580 ``persist_state="session"``, which keeps the value alive through the runs 

1581 where the popover isn't open (ENG-36).""" 

1582 for idx, _ in _COMPARE_SCANPATHS: 

1583 _pin(f"cmp{idx}_fix_color", compare_palette_color(idx)) 

1584 _pin(f"cmp{idx}_saccade_color", compare_palette_color(idx)) 

1585 _pin(f"cmp{idx}_saccade_style", "Solid") 

1586 _pin(f"cmp{idx}_saccade_width", DEFAULT_SACCADE_WIDTH) 

1587 _pin(f"cmp{idx}_marker_size_range", DEFAULT_MARKER_SIZE_RANGE) 

1588 # VIZ-6: per-scanpath marker alpha (replaces the per-scanpath hollow 

1589 # checkbox). Default 0.7 matches the single-trial default so overlapping 

1590 # fixations show through. `cmp{idx}_hollow` kept seeded for saved-config / 

1591 # deep-link backward compatibility (no widget renders it anymore). 

1592 _pin(f"cmp{idx}_opacity", 0.7) 

1593 _pin(f"cmp{idx}_hollow", False) 

1594

1628def _render_compare_saccade_styles() -> None: 

1629 """Per-scanpath *saccade* styling for the two-trial comparison — rendered 

1630 inside the Saccade-style popover (when comparing).""" 

1631 st.caption("Per-scanpath (comparison)")

1650 min_value=SACCADE_WIDTH_BOUNDS[0],
