1652 step=0.5, 

1653 slider_format="%.1f px", 

1654 number_format="%.1f", 

1655 ) 

1656 

1657 

1658def _collect_compare_styles() -> tuple[dict, dict]: 

1659 """Build the ``(style_a, style_b)`` dicts the comparison figure consumes from 

1660 the ``cmp{idx}_*`` session keys (rendered under each layer's popover).""" 

1661 styles: list[dict] = [] 

1662 for idx, _ in _COMPARE_SCANPATHS: 

1663 default_color = compare_palette_color(idx) 

1664 styles.append( 

1665 dict( 

1666 # `or default_color` so a falsy ("" / None) value can never escape 

1667 # as a colour (defensive against the color-picker black desync). 

1668 fix_color=st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_fix_color") or default_color, 

1669 saccade_color=( 

1670 st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_saccade_color") or default_color 

1671 ), 

1672 saccade_style=SACCADE_DASH_OPTIONS.get( 

1673 st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_saccade_style", "Solid"), "solid" 

1674 ), 

1675 saccade_width=float( 

1676 st.session_state.get( 

1677 f"cmp{idx}_saccade_width", DEFAULT_SACCADE_WIDTH 

1678 ) 

1679 ), 

1680 marker_size_range=tuple( 

1681 st.session_state.get( 

1682 f"cmp{idx}_marker_size_range", DEFAULT_MARKER_SIZE_RANGE 

1683 ) 

1684 ), 

1685 hollow=bool(st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_hollow", False)), 

1686 opacity=float(st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_opacity", 1.0)), 

1687 ) 

1688 ) 

1689 return styles[0], styles[1] 

1690 

1691 

1692def _fix_range_max(fixations: Optional[pd.DataFrame]) -> int: 

1693 """Highest 1-based fixation index in ``fixations`` (0 when none).""" 

1694 if ( 

1695 fixations is None 

1696 or fixations.empty 

1697 or "order_in_trial" not in fixations.columns 

1698 ): 

1699 return 0 

1700 top = pd.to_numeric(fixations["order_in_trial"], errors="coerce").max() 

1701 return int(top) if pd.notna(top) else 0 

1702 

1703 

1704def _fix_range_trial_key(fixations: Optional[pd.DataFrame]) -> Optional[tuple]: 

1705 """Identity of the trial the window slider is sizing, or ``None`` if unclear. 

1706 

1707 Used only to notice a *trial change*; a frame that isn't a single trial (or 

1708 carries no identity columns) returns ``None``, which is treated as "don't 

1709 reset" so an ambiguous frame never silently drops the user's window. 

1710 """ 

1711 if fixations is None or fixations.empty: 

1712 return None 

1713 parts = [] 

1714 for col in ("participant_id", "trial_id"): 

1715 if col not in fixations.columns: 

1716 continue 

1717 values = fixations[col].dropna().unique() 

1718 if len(values) != 1: 

1719 return None 

1720 parts.append(str(values[0])) 

1721 return tuple(parts) or None 

1722 

1723 

1724def _render_fix_range_slider(fixations: Optional[pd.DataFrame]) -> None: 

1725 """Render the VIZ-7 fixation-index window slider (``single_fix_range``). 

1726 

1727 The slider value persists across trial changes (which shift ``max_fix``), so 

1728 it is seeded/clamped via session_state *only* (no ``value=`` arg) to stay 

1729 inside ``[1, max_fix]`` — a stored out-of-range value would otherwise raise. 

1730 This is the single fixation-index control for the app; the Comparisons subtab 

1731 deliberately has none of its own (ENG-8). A trial with fewer than two 

1732 fixations can't host a range slider (a one-value slider throws in the 

1733 browser), so the window is cleared to ``None`` (the full, unsliced trial). 

1734 

1735 **Scope.** A window is per-trial by default: picking another trial shows all 

1736 of that trial's fixations again, because a range like "fixations 5–20" rarely 

1737 means the same thing on a different reading. The *Apply to all trials* 

1738 checkbox opts into the sticky behaviour (the window is re-applied to every 

1739 trial, clamped to each one's length). 

1740 

1741 The checkbox is deliberately **UI-only** state (cf. ``share_identity_mode``), 

1742 because what it governs — what happens to the window when you select a 

1743 *different* trial — has no referent on the other three surfaces: a share link, 

1744 a ``render`` invocation and an ``api.plot_scanpath`` call each address one 

1745 explicit trial, and ``api``'s ``fix_index_range`` is a per-call argument 

1746 rather than sticky state. If it is ever persisted into a saved config it must 

1747 be added to ``session_keys.PLOT_CONFIG_STATE_KEYS``. 

1748 

1749 Note ``single_fix_range`` *itself* currently reaches only the UI and the 

1750 headless API — there is no ``fix_range`` URL param and 

1751 ``tabs._build_studio_config`` doesn't write one — so a window is not 

1752 shareable today. That is a pre-existing VIZ-7 gap, not something this 

1753 checkbox introduces; wiring it up would not change the reasoning above. 

1754 """ 

1755 if fixations is None: 

1756 return 

1757 max_fix = _fix_range_max(fixations) 

1758 if max_fix < 2: 

1759 # Nothing meaningful to window — clear any stale stored range so the 

1760 # plot isn't filtered by a window the slider can no longer show. 

1761 if st.session_state.get("single_fix_range") is not None: 

1762 st.session_state["single_fix_range"] = None 

1763 st.session_state["single_fix_range_user_set"] = False 

1764 return 

1765 # Notice a trial change *before* resolving the stored window: in per-trial 

1766 # mode, un-freezing the window is what makes the `user_set is False` branch 

1767 # below expand it to the new trial's full range. 

1768 all_trials = bool(st.session_state.get("single_fix_range_all_trials", False)) 

1769 trial_key = _fix_range_trial_key(fixations) 

1770 if trial_key is not None: 

1771 previous = st.session_state.get("_fix_range_trial") 

1772 st.session_state["_fix_range_trial"] = trial_key 

1773 if previous is not None and previous != trial_key and not all_trials: 

1774 st.session_state["single_fix_range_user_set"] = False 

1775 stored = st.session_state.get("single_fix_range") 

1776 user_set = st.session_state.get("single_fix_range_user_set") 

1777 if stored is None: 

1778 st.session_state["single_fix_range"] = (1, max_fix) 

1779 st.session_state["single_fix_range_user_set"] = False 

1780 elif user_set is False: 

1781 # BUG-16: an untouched auto-default follows the selected trial and always 

1782 # expands to its full range. Only a widget interaction freezes a window. 

1783 st.session_state["single_fix_range"] = (1, max_fix) 

1784 elif isinstance(stored, (tuple, list)) and len(stored) == 2: 

1785 # A value supplied before this widget first renders (test seam, restored 

1786 # session, or future deep link) is explicit and should be preserved. 

1787 st.session_state.setdefault("single_fix_range_user_set", True) 

1788 lo = max(1, min(int(stored[0]), max_fix)) 

1789 hi = max(lo, min(int(stored[1]), max_fix)) 

1790 st.session_state["single_fix_range"] = (lo, hi) 

1791 else: 

1792 st.session_state["single_fix_range"] = (1, max_fix) 

1793 st.session_state["single_fix_range_user_set"] = False 

1794 

1795 def _mark_fix_range_user_set() -> None: 

1796 st.session_state["single_fix_range_user_set"] = True 

1797 

1798 _range_slider( 

1799 st, 

1800 "Fixation index range", 

1801 key="single_fix_range", 

1802 persist_state="session", 

1803 min_value=1, 

1804 max_value=max_fix, 

1805 on_change=_mark_fix_range_user_set, 

1806 help="Draw only fixations whose index falls in this range (their " 

1807 "saccades follow). The chips and panels still describe the full trial; " 

1808 "the bulk (multiple-trial) export is unaffected.", 

1809 ) 

1810 # Seeded via `_VIZ_WIDGET_DEFAULTS`, so no `value=` here (see `_pin`). 

1811 st.checkbox( 

1812 "Apply to all trials", 

1813 key="single_fix_range_all_trials", 

1814 persist_state="session", 

1815 help="**Off** (default) — the window belongs to this trial; picking " 

1816 "another trial shows all of its fixations again. **On** — keep the same " 

1817 "index window as you move through trials, clamped to each trial's " 

1818 "length (a shorter trial narrows it). Either way **Compare** windows " 

1819 "both scanpaths by the same range, since the two readings share one " 

1820 "index axis there.", 

1821 ) 

1822 

1823 

1824def _seed_viz_state( 

1825 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

1826 base_font_size: int, 

1827 words: Optional[pd.DataFrame], 

1828) -> tuple[List[str], List[str], List[str]]: 

1829 """Seed every viz widget's session_state default (pure — renders nothing). 

1830 

1831 Both ``sidebar_controls`` (which renders the widgets) and 

1832 ``viz_settings_from_state`` (the non-rendering reader used by the Corpus view 

1833 and the Save & restore panel) call this first, so the controls and their 

1834 consumers can't drift. The widgets render WITHOUT a ``value=``/``index=`` 

1835 argument and rely on these defaults, which keeps their keys programmatically 

1836 settable (deep links / plot-config restore) without Streamlit's "default 

1837 value but also set via Session State API" warning. 

1838 

1839 Seeding only — keeping a stored value alive through a run where its widget 

1840 doesn't render is the widgets' own ``persist_state="session"`` (ENG-36), so 

1841 this is safe to call both before rendering (``sidebar_controls``) and after 

1842 (``app.main`` re-reads the settings once the rail has rendered, where writing 

1843 a widget key would raise). Returns ``(color_fields, numeric_fields, 

1844 highlight_options)`` for the caller to reuse. 

1845 """ 

1846 for _key, _default in _VIZ_WIDGET_DEFAULTS.items(): 

1847 _pin(_key, _default) 

1848 _pin("global_marker_size_range", (8, 24)) 

1849 _seed_compare_styles() 

1850 

1851 color_fields = color_field_options(trial_fixations) 

1852 _drop_stale("global_color_by", color_fields) 

1853 # VIZ-17: one flat colour by default — see `color_field_options`. 

1854 _pin("global_color_by", UNIFORM_COLOR_FIELD) 

1855 

1856 numeric_fields = numeric_field_options(trial_fixations) 

1857 if numeric_fields: 

1858 x_default = "x" if "x" in numeric_fields else numeric_fields[0] 

1859 y_default = ( 

1860 "y" 

1861 if "y" in numeric_fields 

1862 else numeric_fields[min(1, len(numeric_fields) - 1)] 

1863 ) 

1864 _drop_stale("global_x_field", numeric_fields) 

1865 _pin("global_x_field", x_default) 

1866 _drop_stale("global_y_field", numeric_fields) 

1867 _pin("global_y_field", y_default) 

1868 

1869 # Highlight-column default + stale-clear run every time (even when the Text 

1870 # styling popover isn't rendered this run) so a restored config on data with 

1871 # no boolean columns can't carry a dangling pick. 

1872 highlight_options = highlight_column_options(words) 

1873 _drop_stale("global_highlight_column", highlight_options) 

1874 if highlight_options: 

1875 _pin( 

1876 "global_highlight_column", 

1877 "is_in_aspan" 

1878 if "is_in_aspan" in highlight_options 

1879 else highlight_options[0], 

1880 ) 

1881 

1882 # VIZ-26: arbitrary multi-field word/fixation hover. The legacy one-measure 

1883 # key remains as a fallback for old links/configs, but new surfaces write the 

1884 # explicit lists. 

1885 word_hover_options = hover_field_options(words, words=True) 

1886 fix_hover_options = hover_field_options(trial_fixations) 

1887 _drop_stale_multi("global_word_hover_fields", word_hover_options) 

1888 _drop_stale_multi("global_fixation_hover_fields", fix_hover_options) 

1889 if "global_word_hover_fields" not in st.session_state: 

1890 legacy = st.session_state.get( 

1891 "global_word_hover_measure", "total_fixation_duration_ms" 

1892 ) 

1893 default_word_hover = ["text", "word_id", "line_idx"] 

1894 if legacy: 

1895 default_word_hover.append(legacy) 

1896 _pin( 

1897 "global_word_hover_fields", 

1898 [field for field in default_word_hover if field in word_hover_options], 

1899 ) 

1900 if "global_fixation_hover_fields" not in st.session_state: 

1901 _pin( 

1902 "global_fixation_hover_fields", 

1903 [ 

1904 field 

1905 for field in ("order_in_trial", "duration_ms", "word_id") 

1906 if field in fix_hover_options 

1907 ], 

1908 ) 

1909 return color_fields, numeric_fields, highlight_options 

1910 

1911 

1912def _collect_viz_settings( 

1913 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

1914 words: Optional[pd.DataFrame], 

1915 *, 

1916 numeric_fields: Optional[List[str]] = None, 

1917 highlight_options: Optional[List[str]] = None, 

1918) -> Dict: 

1919 """Build the viz-settings dict from session_state (pure — renders nothing). 

1920 

1921 The single source of truth for the dict the figure builders consume, so the 

1922 rendered controls (``sidebar_controls``) and the non-rendering reader 

1923 (``viz_settings_from_state``) return identical shapes. Conditionally-applied 

1924 fields (colour ranges, the highlight column, saccade arrows) are gated here 

1925 exactly as the widgets gate them, so a stored value for an off layer doesn't 

1926 leak into the figure. ``compare_style_a``/``_b`` are ``None``; the rendering 

1927 path fills them in when the comparison toggle is on. 

1928 """ 

1929 ss = st.session_state 

1930 if highlight_options is None: 

1931 highlight_options = highlight_column_options(words) 

1932 

1933 show_fix = bool(ss.get("global_show_fix")) 

1934 show_saccades = bool(ss.get("global_show_saccades")) 

1935 show_heatmap = bool(ss.get("global_show_heatmap")) 

1936 show_labels = bool(ss.get("global_show_labels")) 

1937 color_by = ss.get("global_color_by") 

1938 

1939 # Fixation colour range only applies when fixations are shown AND coloured by 

1940 # a numeric column with a valid spread — mirror the widget's gate. 

1941 fixation_color_range = None 

1942 if ( 

1943 show_fix 

1944 and color_by in trial_fixations.columns 

1945 and pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(trial_fixations[color_by]) 

1946 ): 

1947 cmin, cmax = trial_fixations[color_by].min(), trial_fixations[color_by].max() 

1948 if pd.notna(cmin) and pd.notna(cmax): 

1949 # Clamp to the same [floor(min), ceil(max)] bounds the rendered slider 

1950 # uses, so the non-rendering reader can't leak a stale out-of-bounds 

1951 # range (cmax_eff mirrors the slider's `cmax if cmax > cmin else +1`). 

1952 lo = float(math.floor(cmin)) 

1953 hi = float(math.ceil(cmax)) 

1954 hi = hi if hi > lo else lo + 1.0 

1955 fixation_color_range = _clamped_pair( 

1956 ss.get("global_fixation_color_range"), lo, hi 

1957 ) 

1958 

1959 # Heatmap colour range only applies for the duration-weighted heatmap. 

1960 heatmap_range = None 

1961 if ( 

1962 show_heatmap 

1963 and ss.get("global_heatmap_metric") == "duration_ms" 

1964 and "duration_ms" in trial_fixations.columns 

1965 ): 

1966 heat = trial_fixations["duration_ms"] 

1967 if len(heat) > 0 and pd.notna(heat.min()) and pd.notna(heat.max()): 

1968 lo = float(math.floor(heat.min())) 

1969 hi = float(math.ceil(heat.max())) 

1970 hi = hi if hi > lo else lo + 1.0 

1971 heatmap_range = _clamped_pair(ss.get("global_heatmap_color_range"), lo, hi) 

1972 

1973 # Fixation-index window (VIZ-7): a (start, end) tuple over `order_in_trial`, 

1974 # or None for the full trial. Read straight from the slider's session key; 

1975 # the rendering path clamps it to the trial's fixation count, and the 

1976 # non-rendering Corpus reader simply leaves it None (it never windows). 

1977 fix_index_range = None 

1978 _fr = ss.get("single_fix_range") 

1979 if isinstance(_fr, (tuple, list)) and len(_fr) == 2: 

1980 fix_index_range = (int(_fr[0]), int(_fr[1])) 

1981 

1982 # Highlight column only applies when Text is shown and a span style is active. 

1983 critical_span_style = ss.get("global_critical_span_style", "Mark text") 

1984 highlight_column = None 

1985 if show_labels and critical_span_style != "None" and highlight_options: 

1986 candidate = ss.get("global_highlight_column") 

1987 highlight_column = candidate if candidate in highlight_options else None 

1988 

1989 # Background colour comes from the Experimental Setup picker (read here so it 

1990 # flows into the figure via viz_settings). 

1991 bg_options = list(BACKGROUND_PRESETS.keys()) + ["Custom…"] 

1992 bg_choice = ss.get("global_bg_choice", bg_options[0]) 

1993 if bg_choice == "Custom…": 

1994 background_color = ss.get("global_bg_custom", DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_COLOR) 

1995 else: 

1996 background_color = BACKGROUND_PRESETS.get( 

1997 bg_choice, BACKGROUND_PRESETS[bg_options[0]] 

1998 ) 

1999 

2000 return dict( 

2001 show_words=bool(ss.get("global_show_words")), 

2002 show_labels=show_labels, 

2003 show_fix=show_fix, 

2004 show_order=bool(ss.get("global_show_order")), 

2005 show_saccades=show_saccades, 

2006 # Arrows are a saccade sub-layer: never report them on when saccades off. 

2007 show_saccade_arrows=bool(ss.get("global_show_saccade_arrows")) 

2008 and show_saccades, 

2009 show_heatmap=show_heatmap, 

2010 # `or default` (not get-default) so a segmented_control deselect → None 

2011 # falls back instead of propagating None into the figure builders. 

2012 heatmap_style=ss.get("global_heatmap_style") or "Word boxes", 

2013 heatmap_norm=ss.get("global_heatmap_norm") or "Linear", 

2014 duration_mass_sigma_chars=float( 

2015 ss.get("global_duration_mass_sigma_chars", 1.0) 

2016 ), 

2017 show_raw_gaze=bool(ss.get("global_show_raw_gaze")), 

2018 show_stimulus_image=bool(ss.get("global_show_stimulus_image")), 

2019 # VIZ-4: image-stimulus opacity (applies to dataset + uploaded images) and 

2020 # the uploaded image's data URI (session-only; set by sidebar_controls). 

2021 stimulus_image_opacity=float(ss.get("global_stimulus_image_opacity", 1.0)), 

2022 stimulus_image_upload_uri=ss.get("_stimulus_image_upload_uri"), 

2023 # VIZ-4: manual image alignment (origin nudge + size scale). 

2024 stimulus_image_offset_x=float(ss.get("global_stimulus_image_offset_x", 0.0)), 

2025 stimulus_image_offset_y=float(ss.get("global_stimulus_image_offset_y", 0.0)), 

2026 stimulus_image_scale=float(ss.get("global_stimulus_image_scale", 1.0)), 

2027 color_by=color_by, 

2028 heatmap_metric=ss.get("global_heatmap_metric") or "duration_ms", 

2029 x_field=ss.get("global_x_field"), 

2030 y_field=ss.get("global_y_field"), 

2031 marker_size_range=tuple(ss.get("global_marker_size_range", (8, 24))), 

2032 order_font_size=ss.get("global_order_font_size"), 

2033 order_font_color=ss.get("global_order_font_color"), 

2034 show_colorbars=bool(ss.get("global_show_colorbars")), 

2035 fit_to_monitor=bool(ss.get("global_fit_to_monitor")), 

2036 show_coordinate_grid=bool(ss.get("global_show_coordinate_grid")), 

2037 coordinate_grid_auto=bool(ss.get("global_coordinate_grid_auto", True)), 

2038 coordinate_grid_spacing=( 

2039 None 

2040 if bool(ss.get("global_coordinate_grid_auto", True)) 

2041 else float(ss.get("global_coordinate_grid_spacing", 100.0)) 

2042 ), 

2043 fixation_color_range=fixation_color_range, 

2044 heatmap_range=heatmap_range, 

2045 fixation_colorscale=ss.get("global_fixation_colorscale") 

2046 or DEFAULT_FIXATION_COLORSCALE, 

2047 heatmap_colorscale=ss.get("global_heatmap_colorscale") 

2048 or DEFAULT_HEATMAP_COLORSCALE, 

2049 critical_span_style=critical_span_style, 

2050 highlight_column=highlight_column, 

2051 saccade_color=ss.get("global_saccade_color", SACCADE_COLOR), 

2052 saccade_style=ss.get("global_saccade_style") or "Solid", 

2053 saccade_width=float(ss.get("global_saccade_width") or DEFAULT_SACCADE_WIDTH), 

2054 # VIZ-8: colour-by-reading-type mode + the per-class palette + optional 

2055 # colour-key legend. 

2056 saccade_color_mode=ss.get("global_saccade_color_mode") or "Uniform", 

2057 saccade_type_legend=bool(ss.get("global_saccade_type_legend", True)), 

2058 saccade_class_colors={ 

2059 cls_name: ss.get( 

2060 f"global_saccade_class_color_{cls_name}", SACCADE_CLASS_COLORS[cls_name] 

2061 ) 

2062 for cls_name in SACCADE_CLASS_EDITABLE 

2063 }, 

2064 # VIZ-31: the reading-class filter. Ordered by SACCADE_CLASS_ORDER (not by 

2065 # click order) so the same selection always produces the same figure key, 

2066 # and unknown names are dropped — a stale link must not smuggle a class 

2067 # the build no longer classifies into the builder. An *empty* selection 

2068 # reads as "no filter", not "draw nothing": hiding the layer entirely is 

2069 # what the Saccades toggle above the filter is for, and a cleared 

2070 # multiselect that blanks the figure reads as a bug. 

2071 saccade_classes=[ 

2072 cls_name 

2073 for cls_name in SACCADE_CLASS_ORDER 

2074 if cls_name in set(ss.get("global_saccade_classes") or SACCADE_CLASS_ORDER) 

2075 ], 

2076 # VIZ-9: linear-reading mode (arced saccades + snap fixations above words). 

2077 saccade_render_mode=ss.get("global_saccade_render_mode") or "Straight", 

2078 fixation_snap_to_word=bool(ss.get("global_fixation_snap_to_word")), 

2079 illustration_label=ss.get("global_illustration_label") or "Auto", 

2080 # VIZ-10: autoplay the animated replay on load (default on). 

2081 anim_autoplay=bool(ss.get("global_anim_autoplay", True)), 

2082 # VIZ-11 follow-up: the animation frame grid (smoothness vs. frame count). 

2083 anim_grid_step_ms=float(ss.get("global_anim_grid_step_ms", 100) or 100), 

2084 anim_max_frames=int(ss.get("global_anim_max_frames", 360) or 360), 

2085 hollow_fixations=bool(ss.get("global_hollow_fixations")), 

2086 fixation_opacity=float(ss.get("global_fixation_opacity", 1.0)), 

2087 # VIZ-17 uniform fixation colour + VIZ-15 marker shape. 

2088 fixation_color=ss.get("global_fixation_color") or DEFAULT_FIXATION_COLOR, 

2089 fixation_symbol=ss.get("global_fixation_symbol") or DEFAULT_FIXATION_SYMBOL, 

2090 # VIZ-18: the active palette name — *derived* from the colour keys above 

2091 # rather than read back from the selector, so a hand-edited figure is 

2092 # reported as `Custom` on every surface instead of carrying a palette 

2093 # name it no longer matches. The colours themselves ride in the 

2094 # individual keys, so `Custom` restores exactly; the name is only there 

2095 # for the picker to come back on the right entry and for export captions. 

2096 palette=_active_palette() or CUSTOM_PALETTE, 

2097 fix_index_range=fix_index_range, 

2098 highlight_text_color=ss.get("global_highlight_text_color"), 

2099 text_color=ss.get("global_text_color", WORD_LABEL_COLOR), 

2100 color_by_line=color_by == "line", 

2101 # Fixation classification (PRE-2) + compare-overlay legend (CMP-2). 

2102 fixation_flags=_collect_fixation_flags(), 

2103 show_compare_legend=bool(ss.get("global_show_compare_legend")), 

2104 span_border_color=ss.get("global_span_border_color", "#000000"), 

2105 colorbar_orientation=ss.get("global_colorbar_orientation") or "Vertical", 

2106 colorbar_tickangle=int(ss.get("global_colorbar_tickangle") or 0), 

2107 colorbar_tickfont_size=int(ss.get("global_colorbar_tickfont_size") or 12), 

2108 background_color=background_color, 

2109 compare_style_a=None, 

2110 compare_style_b=None, 

2111 word_hover_measure=ss.get( 

2112 "global_word_hover_measure", "total_fixation_duration_ms" 

2113 ), 

2114 word_hover_fields=list(ss.get("global_word_hover_fields") or []), 

2115 fixation_hover_fields=list(ss.get("global_fixation_hover_fields") or []), 

2116 # PRE-3: in-place drift correction. `tabs._drift_corrected` applies it once 

2117 # above the render-mode split, so it reaches all three builders (VIZ-23); 

2118 # only the connector layer is still static-figure-only. 

2119 align_algorithm=ss.get("global_align_algorithm") or "Off", 

2120 align_connectors=bool(ss.get("global_align_connectors")) 

2121 and (ss.get("global_align_algorithm") or "Off") != "Off", 

2122 # EXP-5: empty when the toggle is off, regardless of stored pattern text, 

2123 # so turning it off can never leave a stale pattern silently applied. 

2124 title_pattern=( 

2125 ss.get("global_title_pattern") or "" 

2126 if ss.get("global_show_title_caption") 

2127 else "" 

2128 ), 

2129 caption_pattern=( 

2130 ss.get("global_caption_pattern") or "" 

2131 if ss.get("global_show_title_caption") 

2132 else "" 

2133 ), 

2134 ) 

2135 

2136 

2137def viz_settings_from_state( 

2138 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

2139 base_font_size: int, 

2140 words: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, 

2141) -> Dict: 

2142 """Resolve the viz-settings dict from session_state WITHOUT rendering widgets. 

2143 

2144 Used by the views that consume the settings but don't host the controls — the 

2145 Corpus Analysis figures and the Save & restore panel — so they stay in sync 

2146 with the scanpath rail (which renders the actual widgets via 

2147 ``sidebar_controls``) on whatever the user last set. 

2148 """ 

2149 _, numeric_fields, highlight_options = _seed_viz_state( 

2150 trial_fixations, base_font_size, words 

2151 ) 

2152 return _collect_viz_settings( 

2153 trial_fixations, 

2154 words, 

2155 numeric_fields=numeric_fields, 

2156 highlight_options=highlight_options, 

2157 ) 

2158 

2159 

2160def corpus_style_controls( 

2161 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

2162 base_font_size: int, 

2163 *, 

2164 words: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, 

2165 host=None, 

2166 canvas_renderer=None, 

2167) -> Dict: 

2168 """Focused, shared-key styling controls for Corpus Analysis (AN-29). 

2169 

2170 Corpus figures intentionally expose only the palette channels they consume; 

2171 the single-scanpath layer controls remain in the Scanpath rail. Because these 

2172 widgets write the same ``global_*`` keys, Share/config restore, the CLI 

2173 palette, and headless builder parameters stay one contract. 

2174 

2175 ``canvas_renderer`` renders the canvas / text panel here too (VIZ-31). The 

2176 corpus figures are drawn true-to-scale from exactly those values — monitor 

2177 size, fonts, line spacing, background — so the view that consumes them needs 

2178 a way to change them; before VIZ-31 the panel lived in the always-present 

2179 sidebar and was reachable from here for free. 

2180 """ 

2181 _seed_viz_state(trial_fixations, base_font_size, words) 

2182 target = host or st 

2183 with target.expander("🎨 Corpus figure style", expanded=False): 

2184 active = _active_palette() 

2185 options = list(PALETTES) if active else [CUSTOM_PALETTE, *PALETTES] 

2186 st.session_state["global_palette"] = active or CUSTOM_PALETTE 

2187 st.selectbox( 

2188 "Palette", 

2189 options=options, 

2190 key="global_palette", 

2191 persist_state="session", 

2192 on_change=_on_palette_change, 

2193 help="Shared with the Scanpath view and every saved/shareable figure setting.", 

2194 ) 

2195 columns = st.columns(2) 

2196 columns[0].color_picker( 

2197 "Primary series", 

2198 key="global_fixation_color", 

2199 persist_state="session", 

2200 help="First group or profile.", 

2201 ) 

2202 columns[1].color_picker( 

2203 "Secondary series", 

2204 key="global_saccade_color", 

2205 persist_state="session", 

2206 help="Second group.", 

2207 ) 

2208 st.selectbox( 

2209 "Heatmap colorscale", 

2210 options=COLORSCALES, 

2211 key="global_heatmap_colorscale", 

2212 persist_state="session", 

2213 help="Used by word matrices and stimulus heatmaps.", 

2214 ) 

2215 if canvas_renderer is not None: 

2216 canvas_renderer(target) 

2217 return viz_settings_from_state(trial_fixations, base_font_size, words=words) 

2218 

2219 

2220def render_viz_reset(host) -> None: 

2221 """Render the scoped visualization reset popover into ``host``. 

2222 

2223 Full width, like every other trigger in the rail. UX-44's compact ``↺ Reset`` 

2224 pill was for sharing the heading row; BUG-24 moved the control to the foot of 

2225 the rail, where it has a row of its own, so the compact form is gone. 

2226 """ 

2227 reset = host.popover( 

2228 "♻️ Reset settings", 

2229 width="stretch", 

2230 help="Reset visualization settings to their defaults.", 

2231 ) 

2232 reset.caption( 

2233 "Put every visualization control back to the app's defaults. Your " 

2234 "**annotations**, trial filters, column mapping, data source and the " 

2235 "selected trial are kept." 

2236 ) 

2237 reset.button( 

2238 "♻️ Reset visualization", 

2239 key="reset_viz_settings_btn", 

2240 type="primary", 

2241 on_click=reset_viz_settings, 

2242 width="stretch", 

2243 help="Every layer, colour, size and axis control back to its default — " 

2244 "including the settings a Share link put there.", 

2245 ) 

2246 

2247 

2248def sidebar_controls( 

2249 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

2250 base_font_size: int, 

2251 *, 

2252 host=None, 

2253 has_raw_gaze: bool = False, 

2254 has_stimulus_image: bool = False, 

2255 words: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, 

2256 fix_range_fixations: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, 

2257 canvas_renderer=None, 

2258) -> Dict: 

2259 """Render the visualization controls and return the resolved settings dict. 

2260 

2261 Layout (VIZ-31 / UX-44 — grouped so the rail reads by category): 

2262 1. Quick-view presets + Palette at the top: the two controls that get to a 

2263 good figure without opening anything. 

2264 2. Five collapsible sections — **👁️ Fixations** (expanded), then collapsed 

2265 **↗️ Saccades**, **📄 Stimulus**, **🔥 Overlays**, and 

2266 **📐 Figure & canvas** (canvas/text plus axes/labels). 

2267 3. Inside a section: **layer toggle → ⚙️ style → 🧹 filter**, the detail 

2268 popovers shown only while the layer is on. Streamlit nests neither 

2269 expander-in-expander nor popover-in-popover, so an expander holding 

2270 popovers is the only two-level shape available — which is also why 

2271 Fixations and Saccades are peer sections rather than sub-sections of a 

2272 single "Scanpath" group. 

2273 4. **📐 Figure & canvas** follows the same shape with no layer to toggle 

2274 (UX-48): the framing toggle inline, then four popovers — 🖥️ Screen & 

2275 geometry · 🔤 Text & fonts (both from ``canvas_renderer``) · 📊 Axes & 

2276 grid · 🏷️ Title & labels. 

2277 

2278 The sections are created up front (Streamlit lays containers out in creation 

2279 order), so each block below renders into its section without moving in this 

2280 file — see the "Layer groups" comment. 

2281 

2282 ``canvas_renderer`` is an optional ``callable(slot)`` rendering the canvas / 

2283 text panel (``app.render_sidebar_canvas_controls``) into a slot reserved 

2284 between the Overlays and Figure groups. VIZ-31 moved that panel out of the 

2285 sidebar so the figure's fonts, text colour and background sit beside the 

2286 other visual controls; when it is ``None`` (the wizard, the non-rendering 

2287 readers) nothing is drawn there and the panel keeps its own home. 

2288 

2289 ``host`` is the container to render into; it defaults to ``st.sidebar`` for 

2290 backwards compatibility, but the app passes the scanpath rail 

2291 (``tabs.render_single_trial_tab``). The returned dict is built by 

2292 ``_collect_viz_settings`` (shared with ``viz_settings_from_state``) so the 

2293 rendered controls and the non-rendering readers can't drift. 

2294 

2295 ``fix_range_fixations`` is the *selected trial's* fixations, used only to size 

2296 the VIZ-7 fixation-index window slider (its max is that trial's fixation 

2297 count). When omitted, the slider isn't rendered (e.g. the non-rendering 

2298 Corpus reader, which never windows). 

2299 """ 

2300 # can re-push the stored values to the browser (BUG-15 — see `_pin`). 

2301 color_fields, numeric_fields, highlight_options = _seed_viz_state( 

2302 trial_fixations, base_font_size, words 

2303 ) 

2304 if not numeric_fields: 

2305 st.error("No numeric fields found in fixations to map axes.") 

2306 st.stop() 

2307 

2308 # The keyed container is the spotlight-tour target 

2309 # (`.st-key-tour_grp_viz_controls`). Values for controls not rendered this run 

2310 # are read back from session_state by `_collect_viz_settings`, so the returned 

2311 # dict always carries every key the figure builders depend on. 

2312 viz = (host if host is not None else st.sidebar).container( 

2313 key="tour_grp_viz_controls" 

2314 ) 

2315 

2316 # --- Quick views ------------------------------------------------------ 

2317 # Focused presets stay one compact row; Reading-order / Everything 

2318 # are still reachable by toggling layers. The remaining preset keys 

2319 # (`reading_order`, `everything`) stay in `_VIEW_PRESETS` for any deep link. 

2320 viz.caption("Quick views") 

2321 # Side by side to keep the rail short. The active preset (whichever Quick-view 

2322 # preset the current layer toggles match) renders as "primary" so the user can 

2323 # see which view is active at a glance. When neither preset matches (the user 

2324 # has customized layers manually) both buttons render without highlight. 

2325 _active = _active_quick_view() 

2326 _qv = viz.columns(3) 

2327 _qv[0].button( 

2328 "👁️ Scanpath", 

2329 key="viz_view_scanpath", 

2330 type="primary" if _active == "scanpath" else "secondary", 

2331 width="stretch", 

2332 help="Fixations + saccades over the text — the core scanpath.", 

2333 on_click=_apply_view_preset, 

2334 args=("scanpath",), 

2335 ) 

2336 _qv[1].button( 

2337 "🔥 Heatmap", 

2338 key="viz_view_heatmap", 

2339 type="primary" if _active == "heatmap" else "secondary", 

2340 width="stretch", 

2341 help="Fixation-density heatmap over the text, nothing else.", 

2342 on_click=_apply_view_preset, 

2343 args=("heatmap",), 

2344 ) 

2345 _qv[2].button( 

2346 "✏️ Illustration", 

2347 key="viz_view_illustration", 

2348 type="primary" if _active == "illustration" else "secondary", 

2349 width="stretch", 

2350 help="A clean schematic: snapped fixations, arced connectors, and a " 

2351 "uniform visual style.", 

2352 on_click=_apply_view_preset, 

2353 args=("illustration",), 

2354 ) 

2355 # VIZ-31: the Illustration *label* (the publication-disclosure override) now 

2356 # lives in the "📐 Figure & canvas" group below, with the other figure-level 

2357 # presentation settings, rather than as a third top-level row up here. 

2358 

2359 # VIZ-18: these figures end up in papers — printed, sometimes in black & 

2360 # white — and are read by colourblind viewers, so the colour defaults are a 

2361 # choice rather than a constant. Picking one writes the individual colour 

2362 # keys, so every per-element picker below still overrides it — and once one 

2363 # is overridden the selector says **Custom** rather than keeping a name the 

2364 # figure no longer earns (the same rule the Quick-view buttons follow above). 

2365 # `Custom` is offered only while it's true, so the list stays the three real 

2366 # palettes the moment the colours match one again. 

2367 _active = _active_palette() 

2368 _palette_options = list(PALETTES) if _active else [CUSTOM_PALETTE, *PALETTES] 

2369 st.session_state["global_palette"] = _active or CUSTOM_PALETTE 

2370 viz.selectbox( 

2371 "Palette", 

2372 options=_palette_options, 

2373 key="global_palette", 

2374 persist_state="session", 

2375 on_change=_on_palette_change, 

2376 help="Colour defaults for the marks. **Default (colourblind-safe)** uses " 

2377 "the Okabe–Ito hues; **Print / greyscale** drops hue entirely so the " 

2378 "figure survives a black & white print (pair it with a marker shape); " 

2379 "**High contrast** is for projectors. Each one just presets the colour " 

2380 "pickers — change any of them afterwards and this reads **Custom**.", 

2381 ) 

2382 

2383 # Keep the palette controls visually separate from the bordered layer cards. 

2384 # A keyed wrapper gives the spacing a stable, narrowly scoped CSS hook. 

2385 viz.container(key="palette_layers_divider").divider() 

2386 

2387 # Each main layer is an `st.toggle`; the layer's detailed styling lives in a 

2388 # per-layer popover shown only while the layer is on — so the rail shows just 

2389 # the toggles (plus, for fixations, the primary "Color by" control), and the 

2390 # fiddly knobs open in an overlay instead of growing the rail past the plot. 

2391 # Values for off layers are read back from session_state by 

2392 # `_collect_viz_settings`, so the returned dict always carries every key. 

2393 

2394 # VIZ-21: the two view modes (rail → 🎛️ Plot controls, rendered *before* this 

2395 # function) route the figure through different builders, and each ignores a 

2396 # different slice of these controls. Read both flags and gate every affected 

2397 # widget through `_mode_gate` — greyed with a reason, never silently ignored, 

2398 # and never with its stored value rewritten. VIZ-23 then made a batch of them 

2399 # live in Animate / Compare, so what remains gated below is the genuinely 

2400 # builder-less set (see CLAUDE.md's setting → render-path table). 

2401 comparing = bool( 

2402 st.session_state.get( 

2403 "_resolved_comparing", st.session_state.get("single_compare_toggle") 

2404 ) 

2405 ) 

2406 animating = bool( 

2407 st.session_state.get( 

2408 "_resolved_animating", st.session_state.get("single_animate") 

2409 ) 

2410 ) 

2411 # Handy shorthands for the two recurring gates. 

2412 _static_only = dict(in_animation=False, in_compare=False) 

2413 _no_compare = dict(in_compare=False) 

2414 

2415 # --- Layer groups (VIZ-31) -------------------------------------------- 

2416 # The seven layers used to sit as one flat top-to-bottom run of toggles, so 

2417 # the rail opened as ~13 peer rows with no hint that Text / Bounding boxes / 

2418 # Stimulus image describe the *stimulus* while Fixations / Saccades / Raw 

2419 # gaze describe the *recording*. They are now named groups, plus two for how 

2420 # the figure is framed. 

2421 # 

2422 # The groups are created HERE, up front, because Streamlit lays containers 

2423 # out in **creation** order — which lets each block below keep its current 

2424 # position in this file while rendering into whichever group it belongs to. 

2425 # So the visual order is exactly the order of these six lines; the code 

2426 # order further down is unchanged (and irrelevant to the layout). 

2427 # 

2428 # **Section shape.** Each group is `layer toggle → ⚙️ style → 🧹 filter`, the 

2429 # nesting the original wireframe asked for. Streamlit nests neither 

2430 # expander-in-expander nor popover-in-popover, but popover-in-**expander** is 

2431 # allowed — so a section is an expander and its sub-sections are popovers, 

2432 # which is the only two-level shape the framework actually renders. That is 

2433 # also why Fixations and Saccades are *peer* sections rather than one 

2434 # "Scanpath" group holding two sub-sections: the sub-section level is spent 

2435 # on style/filter, where it earns more than on the layer split. 

2436 # 

2437 # Fixations opens because it is the primary layer; Saccades and the less-used 

2438 # groups stay collapsed so the independent rail starts compact. The preset row 

2439 # above still covers the common combinations without opening anything at all. 

2440 fix_grp = viz.expander("👁️ Fixations", expanded=True) 

2441 sac_grp = viz.expander("↗️ Saccades", expanded=False) 

2442 stim_grp = viz.expander("📄 Stimulus", expanded=False) 

2443 ovl_grp = viz.expander("🔥 Overlays", expanded=False) 

2444 # Canvas/text and the former Figure/axes controls share one disclosure: both 

2445 # describe the figure's framing rather than a data layer. The injected canvas 

2446 # renderer writes directly into this expander (not a nested expander), as its 

2447 # own popover sub-groups — see the "Figure & canvas" block below. 

2448 figure_grp = viz.expander("📐 Figure & canvas", expanded=False) 

2449 

2450 # --- Fixations -------------------------------------------------------- 

2451 # The Fixations toggle reaches the static figure AND Compare (CMP-7 — the 

2452 # comparison heatmap is unreadable under two full sets of markers). Only the 

2453 # animated replay ignores it: the replay *is* the fixation trail, so there is 

2454 # nothing left to draw with it off, and `make_scanpath_animation` takes no 

2455 # `show_fixations` argument. 

2456 fix_off_disabled, _ = _mode_gate( 

2457 animating, comparing, in_animation=False, in_compare=True 

2458 ) 

2459 show_fix = fix_grp.toggle( 

2460 "**Fixations**", 

2461 key="global_show_fix", 

2462 persist_state="session", 

2463 disabled=fix_off_disabled, 

2464 help=_gated_help( 

2465 "Draw the fixation markers.", 

2466 "⚠️ Fixations always draw in **Animate** mode — the replay is made " 

2467 "of them. Your setting is kept for the static and comparison " 

2468 "figures; the styling below still applies." 

2469 if fix_off_disabled 

2470 else "", 

2471 ), 

2472 ) 

2473 # …but the styling below is still (partly) live in those modes, so keep the 

2474 # popover reachable even when the (inert) layer toggle reads off. 

2475 if show_fix or fix_off_disabled: 

2476 with fix_grp.popover("⚙️ Style", width="stretch"): 

2477 # The metric that maps to fixation HUE — applies to the static 

2478 # figure, the single animated replay AND the comparison overlay (in 

2479 # compare it colours both scanpaths by the metric; the per-scanpath 

2480 # flat colour below becomes the A/B marker outline). The one path 

2481 # that ignores it is the DUAL animation (Animate + Compare), where 

2482 # the flat A/B colours are all that tells the readings apart. 

2483 metric_disabled, metric_reason = _mode_gate( 

2484 animating, comparing, in_animation=not comparing 

2485 ) 

2486 color_by = st.selectbox( 

2487 "Color fixations by", 

2488 options=color_fields, 

2489 key="global_color_by", 

2490 persist_state="session", 

2491 disabled=metric_disabled, 

2492 help=_gated_help( 

2493 f"The metric mapped to fixation marker hue. **{UNIFORM_COLOR_FIELD}** " 

2494 "(the default) maps nothing — marker *size* already shows fixation " 

2495 "duration, so colour is free for a second variable. Pick a column, " 

2496 "or 'line' to tint each fixation by the text line it lands on " 

2497 "(static plot + single animation only). In compare mode it " 

2498 "colours both scanpaths by this metric.", 

2499 metric_reason, 

2500 ), 

2501 ) 

2502 # VIZ-17: the flat colour, shown only when nothing is mapped to hue. 

2503 # The comparison overlay draws each scanpath in its own colour 

2504 # instead (see "Per-scanpath (comparison)" below), so grey it there. 

2505 if color_by == UNIFORM_COLOR_FIELD: 

2506 _dis, _reason = _mode_gate(animating, comparing, **_no_compare) 

2507 st.color_picker( 

2508 "Fixation color", 

2509 key="global_fixation_color", 

2510 persist_state="session", 

2511 disabled=_dis, 

2512 help=_gated_help( 

2513 "The single colour every fixation marker wears.", _reason 

2514 ), 

2515 ) 

2516 # VIZ-15: marker shape — a channel that survives greyscale printing, 

2517 # so a figure stays readable where hue doesn't (see the Palette 

2518 # picker's **Print / greyscale** option). VIZ-23 gave the comparison 

2519 # builder `fixation_symbol` too, so shape is now a true global: it is 

2520 # the one marker property Compare does NOT override per scanpath 

2521 # (colour / size / opacity / hollow still come from `cmp{idx}_*`). 

2522 st.selectbox( 

2523 "Marker shape", 

2524 options=list(FIXATION_SYMBOLS), 

2525 format_func=lambda s: FIXATION_SYMBOLS[s], 

2526 key="global_fixation_symbol", 

2527 persist_state="session", 

2528 help="Shape of the fixation markers. Unlike colour, shape " 

2529 "still reads in black & white. Applies on all three render " 

2530 "paths, including both compared scanpaths.", 

2531 ) 

2532 # PRE-3: vertical drift correction. Snap each fixation to its assigned 

2533 # text line using one of the Carr et al. (2021) algorithms; "Off" 

2534 # leaves the raw coordinates. VIZ-23 hoisted the correction above the 

2535 # render-mode split in `tabs.py`, so the *algorithm* now applies on all 

2536 # three paths. The CONNECTORS don't: only `make_scanpath_figure` has a 

2537 # connector layer, and drawing a full-length "original position" layer 

2538 # from frame zero would misread as part of the replay's trail. 

2539 static_disabled, static_reason = _mode_gate( 

2540 animating, comparing, **_static_only 

2541 ) 

2542 align_algo = st.selectbox( 

2543 "Drift correction", 

2544 options=_ALIGN_OPTIONS, 

2545 key="global_align_algorithm", 

2546 persist_state="session", 

2547 help="Snap fixations to their assigned text line using a " 

2548 "vertical drift-correction algorithm (Carr et al., 2021). " 

2549 "'Off' shows the raw fixations. See also the 📐 Line " 

2550 "assignment subtab to compare all algorithms side by side.", 

2551 ) 

2552 if align_algo != "Off": 

2553 st.checkbox( 

2554 "Show drift connectors", 

2555 key="global_align_connectors", 

2556 persist_state="session", 

2557 disabled=static_disabled, 

2558 help=_gated_help( 

2559 "Draw a faint line from each fixation's original " 

2560 "position to its corrected (snapped) position.", 

2561 static_reason, 

2562 ), 

2563 ) 

2564 # UX-13: "Snap fixations above words" used to sit flush under the 

2565 # Drift-correction selectbox, which made it read as a 

2566 # drift-correction option. It is not — it's the fixation half of 

2567 # the VIZ-9 *linear-reading schematic* (its partner, arcing 

2568 # saccades, is Saccades → Style → Line shape → Arc). Keep it under 

2569 # Fixations (it moves fixations), but in its own captioned block 

2570 # so the two are never confused. 

2571 st.divider() 

2572 st.caption("Linear-reading schematic") 

2573 # Still `make_scanpath_figure`-only (VIZ-9's `fixation_snap_to_word`), 

2574 # unlike the drift correction above it — hence its own gate. 

2575 st.checkbox( 

2576 "Snap fixations above words", 

2577 key="global_fixation_snap_to_word", 

2578 persist_state="session", 

2579 disabled=static_disabled, 

2580 help=_gated_help( 

2581 "Schematic layout, **not** drift correction: every " 

2582 "fixation is redrawn at the top-centre of the word it landed " 

2583 "on, so the scanpath reads as a diagram rather than as " 

2584 "recorded gaze. Drift correction (above) instead nudges the " 

2585 "raw coordinates onto their true text line. Pairs with " 

2586 "Saccades → ⚙️ Style → Line shape → **Arc**.", 

2587 static_reason, 

2588 ), 

2589 ) 

2590 # Size / opacity are per-scanpath in Compare (`cmp*_marker_size_range` 

2591 # / `cmp*_opacity` always override the global values there). 

2592 _dis, _reason = _mode_gate(animating, comparing, **_no_compare) 

2593 _range_slider( 

2594 st, 

2595 "Size", 

2596 key="global_marker_size_range", 

2597 persist_state="session", 

2598 min_value=4, 

2599 max_value=40, 

2600 disabled=_dis, 

2601 help=_gated_help("Fixation marker size (px).", _reason), 

2602 ) 

2603 _numeric_slider( 

2604 st, 

2605 "Opacity", 

2606 key="global_fixation_opacity", 

2607 persist_state="session", 

2608 min_value=0.1, 

2609 max_value=1.0, 

2610 step=0.05, 

2611 slider_format="%.2f", 

2612 disabled=_dis, 

2613 help=_gated_help( 

2614 "Fixation marker opacity. Lower it so overlapping " 

2615 "fixations show through (1.0 = fully opaque).", 

2616 _reason, 

2617 ), 

2618 ) 

2619 # Only meaningful once a variable is mapped to hue (VIZ-17): with 

2620 # "(uniform)" there is nothing for a colorscale to scale. Follows the

3468# Cached option-list scans for the sidebar filter panel. These run on every 

3469# rerun to populate the multiselects; caching them on a cheap frame fingerprint 

3470# keeps them off the hot path on large corpora (full-column unique() scans). 

3471@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False) 

3472def _participant_options( 

3473 _words: pd.DataFrame, _fixations: pd.DataFrame, cache_key 

3474) -> List[str]: 

3475 return sorted( 

3476 set(_words["participant_id"].dropna().astype(str)) 

3477 | set(_fixations["participant_id"].dropna().astype(str)) 

3478 ) 

3479 

3480 

3481@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False) 

3482def _column_unique_strs(_df: pd.DataFrame, column: str, cache_key) -> List[str]: 

3483 if column not in _df.columns: 

3484 return [] 

3485 # Drop missing values, including the literal "nan" a string-coerced optional 

3486 # field leaves for NaN (e.g. ET2 readers with no recorded gender) — a "nan" 

3487 # filter option would be meaningless. 

3488 values = _df[column].dropna().astype(str).unique() 

3489 return sorted(v for v in values if v.strip().lower() not in ("nan", "none", "<na>")) 

3490 

3491 

3492@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False) 

3493def _column_present_bools(_df: pd.DataFrame, column: str, cache_key) -> frozenset: 

3494 if column not in _df.columns: 

3495 return frozenset() 

3496 return frozenset( 

3497 bool(v) for v in pd.Series(_df[column]).dropna().astype(bool).unique() 

3498 ) 

3499 

3500 

3501def _bool_metadata_filter( 

3502 label: str, 

3503 col: str, 

3504 df: pd.DataFrame, 

3505 true_label: str, 

3506 false_label: str, 

3507 key: str, 

3508 host, 

3509 on_change=None, 

3510) -> None: 

3511 """Render a friendly multiselect for a boolean metadata column. 

3512 

3513 Rendering only — the narrowing value is derived from the widget key by 

3514 ``_compute_trial_filters``. Renders nothing when the column is absent or has 

3515 fewer than two classes.""" 

3516 if col not in df.columns: 

3517 return 

3518 present = _column_present_bools(df, col, cache_key=(frame_fingerprint(df), col)) 

3519 label_to_val = {true_label: True, false_label: False} 

3520 options = [lbl for lbl, val in label_to_val.items() if val in present] 

3521 if len(options) < 2: 

3522 return 

3523 _seed_filter_widget(key, options, options) 

3524 host.multiselect(label, options=options, key=key, on_change=on_change) 

3525 

3526 

3527def _bool_filter_narrowing( 

3528 col: str, df: pd.DataFrame, true_label: str, false_label: str, key: str 

3529) -> Optional[set]: 

3530 """The set of raw bool values to keep for a boolean metadata column, read 

3531 from its widget key — or None when absent / fewer than two classes / the user 

3532 kept everything (no narrowing). The read-side twin of ``_bool_metadata_filter``.""" 

3533 if col not in df.columns: 

3534 return None 

3535 present = _column_present_bools(df, col, cache_key=(frame_fingerprint(df), col)) 

3536 label_to_val = {true_label: True, false_label: False} 

3537 options = [lbl for lbl, val in label_to_val.items() if val in present] 

3538 if len(options) < 2: 

3539 return None 

3540 chosen = st.session_state.get(key) 

3541 if not chosen or set(chosen) == set(options): 

3542 return None 

3543 vals = {label_to_val[c] for c in chosen if c in label_to_val} 

3544 return vals or None

3578_EMPTY_TRIAL_FILTERS: Dict = {

3586 

3587#: Every filter-layer namespace in the app. ``""`` is the main trial pool; 

3588#: ``"cmp"`` is compare mode's scanpath B (CMP-8 §5.2). The empty prefix's 

3589#: clear-sweep uses this to know which keys are *not* its own — without it, 

3590#: "Clear all filters" on A would wipe B too, since ``"filter_"`` is a prefix of 

3591#: ``"cmpfilter_"``. Register a new instance here, not just at its call site. 

3592FILTER_PREFIXES: tuple = ("", "cmp") 

3593 

3594 

3595def read_trial_filters(prefix: str = "") -> Dict: 

3596 """The trial-filter selections to apply this run. 

3597 

3598 ``prefix`` scopes the whole filter layer to one instance (CMP-8 §5.2). The 

3599 default ``""`` is the main pool and leaves every existing call site 

3600 byte-identical; compare mode's scanpath **B** renders with ``prefix="cmp"`` 

3601 so it can be narrowed on *its own* dataset's columns, which A's filters may 

3602 not even have. 

3603 

3604 Computed last run by ``render_trial_filters`` and stashed in a *plain* 

3605 session_state value (not a widget key), so it survives runs where the filter 

3606 panel itself isn't rendered — e.g. when a non-Scanpath view is active under 

3607 the sidebar nav. ``main()`` reads this *before* the tab renders, so filtering 

3608 stays global even though the controls now live in the Trial Selection panel. 

3609 """ 

3610 return dict(st.session_state.get(f"{prefix}_trial_filters", _EMPTY_TRIAL_FILTERS)) 

3611 

3612 

3613def clear_trial_filters(prefix: str = "") -> None: 

3614 """Reset every trial filter to "no constraint" (UX-7's one-click escape). 

3615 

3616 All of them — the Narrow-by multiselects, the More-popover condition filters, 

3617 and the annotation filters — live under the ``filter_`` key prefix, so 

3618 dropping those keys is the whole reset: each widget re-seeds to its own empty 

3619 default (an empty multiselect means *no* narrowing) on the next render. The 

3620 derived results and the cross-view mirror are cleared with them so the same 

3621 run already sees an unfiltered pool. 

3622 

3623 Safe to call as a button ``on_click``: callbacks run before the rerun 

3624 instantiates the widgets, so removing their keys doesn't trip Streamlit's 

3625 "set after instantiation" guard. 

3626 """ 

3627 for key in _own_filter_keys(prefix): 

3628 del st.session_state[key] 

3629 st.session_state.pop(f"{prefix}_trial_filters", None) 

3630 st.session_state.pop(f"{prefix}_trial_filters_raw", None) 

3631 

3632 

3633def _own_filter_keys(prefix: str) -> list: 

3634 """Filter widget keys belonging to ``prefix`` and to no *longer* prefix. 

3635 

3636 The sweep used to be prefix-blind, which is fine while there is one filter 

3637 set and wrong the moment there are two: ``"filter_"`` is a prefix of 

3638 ``"cmpfilter_"``, so clearing A's filters would silently wipe B's as well. 

3639 Matching forwards is not enough — the empty prefix has to explicitly skip 

3640 keys carrying a known namespace. 

3641 """ 

3642 own = f"{prefix}filter_" 

3643 foreign = tuple(f"{p}filter_" for p in FILTER_PREFIXES if p and p != prefix) 

3644 return [ 

3645 k 

3646 for k in list(st.session_state) 

3647 if str(k).startswith(own) and not (prefix == "" and str(k).startswith(foreign)) 

3648 ] 

3649 

3650 

3651def reset_viz_settings() -> None: 

3652 """Put every visualization setting back to the app's defaults (UX-26). 

3653 

3654 The mechanism is ``clear_trial_filters``' — delete the widget keys and let 

3655 each control re-seed from ``_VIZ_WIDGET_DEFAULTS`` (plus the data-dependent 

3656 defaults `_seed_viz_state` computes) on the next render — so it must run as a 

3657 button ``on_click``: callbacks run before the rerun instantiates the widgets, 

3658 which is what keeps deleting their keys clear of Streamlit's "set after 

3659 instantiation" guard. 

3660 

3661 The key set is the honest inventory of what *visualization settings* means: 

3662 every ``global_*`` key, the per-scanpath compare styles 

3663 (``session_keys.compare_state_keys``), and the fixation-window pair the rail 

3664 owns. ``session_keys.PLOT_CONFIG_STATE_KEYS`` is folded in so a setting that 

3665 is restorable-but-not-currently-rendered is reset too. Deliberately NOT 

3666 touched: the trial selection, the annotations (user-authored content, not a 

3667 setting), the column mapping, and the data source. 

3668 

3669 Deep links re-apply: ``url_state._apply_url_preset`` seeds from 

3670 ``st.query_params`` at the top of every rerun, so on a page opened from a 

3671 Share link, deleting the keys alone would let the link reinstate itself on 

3672 the very next run. The viz params are stripped from the query string here; 

3673 the selection params (source / participant / trial) are left, so a reset 

3674 keeps you on the trial you were looking at. 

3675 """ 

3676 from . import session_keys as _sk 

3677 

3678 keys = set(_sk.PLOT_CONFIG_STATE_KEYS) 

3679 keys |= set(_sk.compare_state_keys(0)) | set(_sk.compare_state_keys(1)) 

3680 keys |= {k for k in st.session_state if str(k).startswith("global_")} 

3681 keys |= {"single_fix_range", "single_fix_range_all_trials"} 

3682 for key in keys: 

3683 st.session_state.pop(key, None) 

3684 # Re-seeding is source-driven for these two (see app.seed_canvas_state); 

3685 # dropping the guard makes the canvas / font snap back to the source's 

3686 # authoritative monitor on the next run rather than sticking at the old size. 

3687 st.session_state.pop("_canvas_seeded_for", None) 

3688 st.session_state.pop("_font_seeded_for", None) 

3689 st.session_state.pop("_palette_picked", None) 

3690 st.session_state.pop(_PRE_ILLUSTRATION_STATE, None) 

3691 for param in _sk.URL_PRESET_PARAMS: 

3692 st.query_params.pop(param, None) 

3693 

3694 

3695def clear_trial_filter(*keys: str, prefix: str = "") -> None: 

3696 """Reset *one* trial filter (UX-7) — the same mechanism as the reset-all. 

3697 

3698 Deleting the widget's key is the correct reset for every filter shape here, 

3699 because each re-seeds to its own "no constraint" default on the next render: 

3700 an empty multiselect for Narrow-by, *all* values selected for a condition, 

3701 unchecked for Favorites. Safe as a button ``on_click`` for the same reason 

3702 :func:`clear_trial_filters` is. 

3703 """ 

3704 for key in keys: 

3705 st.session_state.pop(key, None) 

3706 st.session_state.pop(f"{prefix}_trial_filters", None) 

3707 st.session_state.pop(f"{prefix}_trial_filters_raw", None) 

3708 

3709 

3710def has_active_trial_filters(prefix: str = "") -> bool: 

3711 """Whether any trial filter is currently narrowing the pool.""" 

3712 f = read_trial_filters(prefix) 

3713 return bool( 

3714 f.get("participants") 

3715 or f.get("metadata") 

3716 or f.get("favorites_only") 

3717 or f.get("required_tags") 

3718 or f.get("excluded_tags") 

3719 ) 

3720 

3721 

3722# --- Trial summary chips (the "Field = Value" strip above the plot) ---------- 

3723_CHIP_TEXT_ID_COLS = ( 

3724 "unique_text_id", 

3725 "text_id", 

3726 "unique_paragraph_id", 

3727 "paragraph_id", 

3728) 

3729# Sensible default chips: trial identity + the common OneStop conditions + the 

3730# computed trial-level summary stats (which the chips replaced the Trial Info tab 

3731# with). The "@"-prefixed keys are virtual fields computed per trial in 

3732# `tabs._render_trial_condition_chips` (see SUMMARY_CHIP_FIELDS). 

3733_CHIP_DEFAULT_CONDITIONS = [ 

3734 "difficulty_level", 

3735 "question_preview", 

3736 "repeated_reading_trial", 

3737 "is_correct", 

3738 # MultiplEYE facets + reader metadata (present only for that corpus). 

3739 "genre", 

3740 "session", 

3741 "pp_age", 

3742 "pp_gender", 

3743] 

3744# Virtual chip fields → label. These are computed per trial (not data columns), 

3745# always trial-level, and folded in from the former Trial Info tab's summary. 

3746SUMMARY_CHIP_FIELDS = { 

3747 "@reading_time_s": "Total reading time (s)", 

3748 "@word_count": "Number of words", 

3749 "@fixation_count": "Number of fixations", 

3750 "@in_text_fixations": "Fixations in word boxes", 

3751} 

3752 

3753 

3754def _trial_level_columns(words: pd.DataFrame, fixations: pd.DataFrame) -> set: 

3755 """Columns that are constant within a trial (so a single chip value is 

3756 meaningful), sampled from the first trial only — cheap, and trial-level-ness 

3757 is essentially a property of the dataset, not the specific trial. A column 

3758 counts as trial-level when it has ≤1 distinct value within that sample trial. 

3759 """ 

3760 level: set = set() 

3761 src = fixations if (fixations is not None and not fixations.empty) else words 

3762 if ( 

3763 src is None 

3764 or src.empty 

3765 or "participant_id" not in src.columns 

3766 or "trial_id" not in src.columns 

3767 ): 

3768 return level 

3769 pid, tid = str(src["participant_id"].iloc[0]), str(src["trial_id"].iloc[0]) 

3770 for frame in (words, fixations): 

3771 if ( 

3772 frame is None 

3773 or frame.empty 

3774 or "participant_id" not in frame.columns 

3775 or "trial_id" not in frame.columns 

3776 ): 

3777 continue 

3778 sub = frame[ 

3779 (frame["participant_id"].astype(str) == pid) 

3780 & (frame["trial_id"].astype(str) == tid) 

3781 ] 

3782 if sub.empty: 

3783 continue 

3784 for col in sub.columns: 

3785 if sub[col].nunique(dropna=True) <= 1: 

3786 level.add(col) 

3787 return level 

3788 

3789 

3790def _chip_field_options(words, fixations, trial_level: set) -> List[str]: 

3791 """Pickable chip fields: participant + a text id + the data's *trial-level* 

3792 columns + the computed summary fields. Non-trial-level columns (per-word / 

3793 per-fixation) are intentionally excluded — a single chip value for them would 

3794 be misleading.""" 

3795 cols: List[str] = [] 

3796 

3797 def add(c: str) -> None: 

3798 if c and c not in cols: 

3799 cols.append(c) 

3800 

3801 if "participant_id" in words.columns or "participant_id" in fixations.columns: 

3802 add("participant_id") 

3803 add(next((c for c in _CHIP_TEXT_ID_COLS if c in words.columns), "")) 

3804 for c in list(words.columns) + list(fixations.columns): 

3805 if c in trial_level: 

3806 add(c) 

3807 cols.extend(SUMMARY_CHIP_FIELDS) 

3808 return cols 

3809 

3810 

3811def _chip_option_label(col: str) -> str: 

3812 """Display label for a chip-field option (identity / virtual / humanized).""" 

3813 if col in SUMMARY_CHIP_FIELDS: 

3814 return SUMMARY_CHIP_FIELDS[col] 

3815 if col == "participant_id": 

3816 return "Participant" 

3817 if col in _CHIP_TEXT_ID_COLS: 

3818 return "Text" 

3819 return col.replace("_", " ").strip().capitalize() 

3820 

3821 

3822def _default_chip_fields(available: List[str]) -> List[str]: 

3823 text_col = next((c for c in _CHIP_TEXT_ID_COLS if c in available), None) 

3824 wanted = ( 

3825 ["participant_id"] 

3826 + ([text_col] if text_col else []) 

3827 + _CHIP_DEFAULT_CONDITIONS 

3828 + list(SUMMARY_CHIP_FIELDS) 

3829 ) 

3830 return [f for f in wanted if f in available] 

3831 

3832 

3833def render_trial_chip_picker( 

3834 words: pd.DataFrame, fixations: pd.DataFrame, host 

3835) -> None: 

3836 """Render the inline **Edit chips** control: choose which ``Field = Value`` 

3837 chips appear above the scanpath and **drag to reorder** them (UX-1 / UX-1a). 

3838 

3839 Two drag buckets — *Shown* (in display order) and *Available* — via 

3840 ``streamlit_sortables.sort_items``: drag a field between buckets to show / hide 

3841 it, and within *Shown* to reorder. The resulting order is written to the plain 

3842 session key ``trial_chip_fields`` (read by ``tabs._render_trial_condition_chips``). 

3843 

3844 Only *trial-level* fields are offered (constant within a trial) plus the 

3845 computed summary stats, so a chip never shows a per-word column whose single 

3846 value would mislead. The trial-level set is computed once (sampling the first 

3847 trial) and cached per column-signature; a **Refresh** button recomputes it. 

3848 Default seeded once (participant + text + common conditions + summary).""" 

3849 # Cache the trial-level field set per column-signature (stable across trials / 

3850 # filters within a dataset), recomputed on a dataset/column change or Refresh. 

3851 signature = (tuple(words.columns), tuple(fixations.columns)) 

3852 cache = st.session_state.get("_trial_level_cache") 

3853 if not cache or cache.get("signature") != signature: 

3854 cache = { 

3855 "signature": signature, 

3856 "fields": _trial_level_columns(words, fixations), 

3857 } 

3858 st.session_state["_trial_level_cache"] = cache 

3859 

3860 available = _chip_field_options(words, fixations, cache["fields"]) 

3861 if not available: 

3862 return 

3863 

3864 # Display labels must be unique to stay invertible: some fields humanize to the 

3865 # same text (e.g. two text-id columns both read "Text"), so disambiguate. 

3866 label_to_key: Dict[str, str] = {} 

3867 key_to_label: Dict[str, str] = {} 

3868 for key in available: 

3869 base = _chip_option_label(key) 

3870 label = base if base not in label_to_key else f"{base} ({key})" 

3871 label_to_key[label] = key 

3872 key_to_label[key] = label 

3873 

3874 # Current selection/order, pruned to what's available + seeded once. 

3875 if "trial_chip_fields" in st.session_state: 

3876 st.session_state["trial_chip_fields"] = [ 

3877 f for f in st.session_state["trial_chip_fields"] if f in available 

3878 ] 

3879 st.session_state.setdefault("trial_chip_fields", _default_chip_fields(available)) 

3880 selected = list(st.session_state["trial_chip_fields"]) 

3881 hidden = [k for k in available if k not in selected] 

3882 

3883 host.caption( 

3884 "Drag fields between **Shown** and **Available**, and reorder within " 

3885 "**Shown** — these chips appear above the scanpath." 

3886 ) 

3887 buckets = [ 

3888 { 

3889 "header": "Shown · drag to reorder", 

3890 "items": [key_to_label[k] for k in selected], 

3891 }, 

3892 {"header": "Available", "items": [key_to_label[k] for k in hidden]}, 

3893 ] 

3894 with host: 

3895 # Key varies with the field universe so the component re-mounts (rather than 

3896 # keeping a stale drag order) when the dataset / columns change. 

3897 result = sort_items( 

3898 buckets, 

3899 multi_containers=True, 

3900 direction="vertical", 

3901 key=f"trial_chip_sort_{abs(hash(signature))}", 

3902 ) 

3903 shown_labels = result[0]["items"] if result else [] 

3904 st.session_state["trial_chip_fields"] = [ 

3905 label_to_key[lbl] for lbl in shown_labels if lbl in label_to_key 

3906 ] 

3907 host.button( 

3908 "🔄 Refresh fields", 

3909 key="trial_chip_refresh", 

3910 help="Re-scan which fields are trial-level (if the offered list looks off " 

3911 "for the current data).", 

3912 on_click=lambda: st.session_state.pop("_trial_level_cache", None), 

3913 ) 

3914 

3915 # UX-28: per-chip colour, generalized from what used to be a handful of 

3916 # hardcoded OneStop column/value special-cases (tabs._chip_color) — any 

3917 # dataset's condition chips can now be highlighted, not just OneStop's. 

3918 # `#EEF2F7` must match `tabs._CHIP_NEUTRAL_BG`: picking it back is how a 

3919 # chip returns to "no override" rather than staying pinned to a colour. 

3920 _neutral = "#EEF2F7" 

3921 shown_now = st.session_state["trial_chip_fields"] 

3922 if shown_now: 

3923 host.caption("Chip colours — optional highlight per shown field.") 

3924 colors = dict(st.session_state.get("trial_chip_colors") or {}) 

3925 for key in shown_now: 

3926 label_col, swatch_col = host.columns([3, 1], vertical_alignment="center") 

3927 label_col.caption(key_to_label[key]) 

3928 picked = swatch_col.color_picker( 

3929 key_to_label[key], 

3930 value=colors.get(key) or _neutral, 

3931 key=f"trial_chip_color_{key}", 

3932 label_visibility="collapsed", 

3933 help="Pick back to the default grey to remove the highlight.", 

3934 ) 

3935 if picked.lower() == _neutral.lower(): 

3936 colors.pop(key, None) 

3937 else: 

3938 colors[key] = picked 

3939 st.session_state["trial_chip_colors"] = colors 

3940 

3941 

3942def _seed_filter_widget( 

3943 key: str, options: list, default: list, *, prefix: str = "" 

3944) -> None: 

3945 """Pre-seed a filter widget's state from the persistent mirror. 

3946 

3947 Filter controls live in the Scanpath tab body, which doesn't render on every 

3948 run (other views under the sidebar nav). Streamlit clears a not-rendered 

3949 widget's key, so on return we re-seed it from ``_trial_filters_raw`` (the last 

3950 selections), dropping any value no longer in ``options`` (e.g. after a dataset 

3951 switch). Setting the key *before* the widget renders avoids the 

3952 default-plus-session-state warning.""" 

3953 if key in st.session_state: 

3954 return 

3955 mirror = st.session_state.get(f"{prefix}_trial_filters_raw", {}) 

3956 if key in mirror: 

3957 kept = [v for v in mirror[key] if v in options] 

3958 st.session_state[key] = kept if kept else list(default) 

3959 else: 

3960 st.session_state[key] = list(default) 

3961 

3962 

3963def _filter_fields_for(words: pd.DataFrame, fixations: pd.DataFrame) -> list: 

3964 """Trial-level condition columns to offer as filters (wizard-chosen for an 

3965 upload, else the built-in defaults present in the data).""" 

3966 filter_fields = st.session_state.get("wizard_filter_fields") 

3967 if filter_fields is None: 

3968 filter_fields = [ 

3969 c 

3970 for c in _DEFAULT_FILTER_FIELDS 

3971 if c in words.columns or c in fixations.columns 

3972 ] 

3973 return filter_fields 

3974 

3975 

3976def _compute_trial_filters( 

3977 words: pd.DataFrame, fixations: pd.DataFrame, *, prefix: str = "" 

3978) -> Dict: 

3979 """Derive the narrowing filter result from the live filter-widget values. 

3980 

3981 Reads the widget keys (filter_participants / filter_<col> / filter_favorites / 

3982 filter_req_tags / filter_exc_tags) — which Streamlit has already updated on the 

3983 rerun the user changed a filter — so the filter applies on the SAME run. The 

3984 on_change callbacks in ``render_trial_filters`` call this *before* the rerun; 

3985 it also runs at the end of that function for no-change runs. Only narrowing 

3986 selections feed the result. 

3987 """ 

3988 result: Dict = { 

3989 "participants": None, 

3990 "metadata": {}, 

3991 # column -> the session key holding it, so "clear just this filter" 

3992 # (UX-7) can reset one widget. Not derivable from the column name: the 

3993 # Narrow-by Text multiselect lands in `metadata` under the *text column* 

3994 # but lives under `filter_text_id`. 

3995 "metadata_keys": {}, 

3996 "favorites_only": False, 

3997 "required_tags": [], 

3998 "excluded_tags": [], 

3999 } 

4000 parts = _participant_options( 

4001 words, 

4002 fixations, 

4003 cache_key=(frame_fingerprint(words), frame_fingerprint(fixations)), 

4004 ) 

4005 if len(parts) > 1: 

4006 sel = st.session_state.get(f"{prefix}filter_participants") 

4007 if sel and len(sel) < len(parts): 

4008 result["participants"] = list(sel) 

4009 # Text narrowing (the "Narrow by → Text" multiselect). Like a categorical 

4010 # condition, but the text id isn't in the condition list, so handle it here. 

4011 text_field, text_frame = _text_field_and_frame(words, fixations) 

4012 if text_field is not None: 

4013 text_vals = _column_unique_strs( 

4014 text_frame, 

4015 text_field, 

4016 cache_key=(frame_fingerprint(text_frame), text_field), 

4017 ) 

4018 sel = st.session_state.get(f"{prefix}filter_text_id") 

4019 if sel and len(text_vals) > 1 and len(sel) < len(text_vals): 

4020 result["metadata"][text_field] = set(sel) 

4021 # UX-7's per-filter clear pops exactly this key, so it must be 

4022 # emitted already-prefixed or clearing one of B's filters no-ops. 

4023 result["metadata_keys"][text_field] = f"{prefix}filter_text_id" 

4024 for col in _filter_fields_for(words, fixations): 

4025 frame = words if col in words.columns else fixations 

4026 if col not in frame.columns: 

4027 continue 

4028 spec = _FILTER_FIELD_LABELS.get(col, {}) 

4029 if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(frame[col]): 

4030 vals = _bool_filter_narrowing( 

4031 col, 

4032 frame, 

4033 spec.get("true", "Yes"), 

4034 spec.get("false", "No"), 

4035 f"{prefix}filter_{col}", 

4036 ) 

4037 if vals is not None: 

4038 result["metadata"][col] = vals 

4039 result["metadata_keys"][col] = f"{prefix}filter_{col}" 

4040 else: 

4041 values = _column_unique_strs( 

4042 frame, col, cache_key=(frame_fingerprint(frame), col) 

4043 ) 

4044 sel = st.session_state.get(f"{prefix}filter_{col}") 

4045 if sel and len(values) > 1 and len(sel) < len(values): 

4046 result["metadata"][col] = set(sel) 

4047 result["metadata_keys"][col] = f"{prefix}filter_{col}" 

4048 result["favorites_only"] = bool( 

4049 st.session_state.get(f"{prefix}filter_favorites", False) 

4050 ) 

4051 result["required_tags"] = list( 

4052 st.session_state.get(f"{prefix}filter_req_tags") or [] 

4053 ) 

4054 result["excluded_tags"] = list( 

4055 st.session_state.get(f"{prefix}filter_exc_tags") or [] 

4056 ) 

4057 return result 

4058 

4059 

4060def _text_field_and_frame(words: pd.DataFrame, fixations: pd.DataFrame): 

4061 """The text/passage id column to narrow by + the frame it lives on (prefer 

4062 fixations, where trials live). ``(None, fixations)`` when no text column.""" 

4063 for field in ("unique_text_id", "text_id"): 

4064 if field in fixations.columns: 

4065 return field, fixations 

4066 if field in words.columns: 

4067 return field, words 

4068 return None, fixations 

4069 

4070 

4071def render_narrow_by( 

4072 words: pd.DataFrame, 

4073 fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

4074 *, 

4075 prefix: str = "", 

4076 text_host=None, 

4077 part_host=None, 

4078) -> None: 

4079 """Inline **Narrow by** multiselects — Text + Participant — that narrow the 

4080 trial pool feeding the picker (the former Browse-by Text/Participant modes, now 

4081 filters). They write the same ``filter_*`` keys the "More" popover uses and 

4082 recompute via ``_compute_trial_filters``, so narrowing applies the same run. 

4083 Start empty = no narrowing; pick values to narrow.""" 

4084 

4085 def _apply() -> None: 

4086 st.session_state[f"{prefix}_trial_filters"] = _compute_trial_filters( 

4087 words, fixations, prefix=prefix 

4088 ) 

4089 

4090 th = text_host if text_host is not None else st 

4091 ph = part_host if part_host is not None else st 

4092 

4093 text_field, text_frame = _text_field_and_frame(words, fixations) 

4094 if text_field is not None: 

4095 text_vals = _column_unique_strs( 

4096 text_frame, 

4097 text_field, 

4098 cache_key=(frame_fingerprint(text_frame), text_field), 

4099 ) 

4100 if len(text_vals) > 1: 

4101 _seed_filter_widget(f"{prefix}filter_text_id", text_vals, [], prefix=prefix) 

4102 th.multiselect( 

4103 "Text", 

4104 options=text_vals, 

4105 key=f"{prefix}filter_text_id", 

4106 on_change=_apply, 

4107 placeholder="All texts", 

4108 label_visibility="collapsed", 

4109 ) 

4110 

4111 parts = _participant_options( 

4112 words, 

4113 fixations, 

4114 cache_key=(frame_fingerprint(words), frame_fingerprint(fixations)), 

4115 ) 

4116 if len(parts) > 1: 

4117 _seed_filter_widget(f"{prefix}filter_participants", parts, [], prefix=prefix) 

4118 ph.multiselect( 

4119 "Participant", 

4120 options=parts, 

4121 key=f"{prefix}filter_participants", 

4122 on_change=_apply, 

4123 placeholder="All participants", 

4124 label_visibility="collapsed", 

4125 ) 

4126 

4127 

4128def render_trial_filters( 

4129 words: pd.DataFrame, fixations: pd.DataFrame, *, prefix: str = "", host=None 

4130) -> Dict: 

4131 """Render the trial-filter controls into ``host`` and persist the selections. 

4132 

4133 Lets the user narrow the trial pool by participant and by categorical 

4134 condition (Hunting/Gathering, difficulty, first/repeated reading, 

4135 correctness) plus annotation state (favorites / tags). Renders into ``host`` 

4136 (the Trial Selection panel; defaults to the sidebar). The narrowing result is 

4137 derived by ``_compute_trial_filters`` and stashed in session_state 

4138 (`_trial_filters`); each widget's ``on_change`` recomputes it *before* the 

4139 rerun so ``main()``'s ``read_trial_filters`` applies the change on the same 

4140 run. The persisted value also survives runs where this panel isn't rendered 

4141 (a non-Scanpath view under the sidebar nav). 

4142 """ 

4143 if host is None: 

4144 host = st.sidebar 

4145 

4146 def _apply() -> None: 

4147 st.session_state[f"{prefix}_trial_filters"] = _compute_trial_filters( 

4148 words, fixations, prefix=prefix 

4149 ) 

4150 

4151 # Text + Participant narrowing now lives in the inline "Narrow by" row 

4152 # (``render_narrow_by``); this popover keeps the condition + annotation filters. 

4153 for col in _filter_fields_for(words, fixations): 

4154 frame = words if col in words.columns else fixations 

4155 if col not in frame.columns: 

4156 continue 

4157 spec = _FILTER_FIELD_LABELS.get(col, {}) 

4158 label = spec.get("label", col.replace("_", " ").strip().title()) 

4159 if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(frame[col]): 

4160 _bool_metadata_filter( 

4161 label, 

4162 col, 

4163 frame, 

4164 spec.get("true", "Yes"), 

4165 spec.get("false", "No"), 

4166 f"{prefix}filter_{col}", 

4167 host, 

4168 on_change=_apply, 

4169 ) 

4170 else: 

4171 values = _column_unique_strs( 

4172 frame, col, cache_key=(frame_fingerprint(frame), col) 

4173 ) 

4174 if len(values) > 1: 

4175 _seed_filter_widget( 

4176 f"{prefix}filter_{col}", values, values, prefix=prefix 

4177 ) 

4178 host.multiselect( 

4179 label, 

4180 options=values, 

4181 key=f"{prefix}filter_{col}", 

4182 on_change=_apply, 

4183 ) 

4184 

4185 host.markdown("**By annotation**") 

4186 if f"{prefix}filter_favorites" not in st.session_state: 

4187 st.session_state[f"{prefix}filter_favorites"] = bool( 

4188 st.session_state.get(f"{prefix}_trial_filters_raw", {}).get( 

4189 f"{prefix}filter_favorites", False 

4190 ) 

4191 ) 

4192 host.checkbox( 

4193 "⭐ Favorites only", key=f"{prefix}filter_favorites", on_change=_apply 

4194 ) 

4195 tags = known_tags() 

4196 if tags: 

4197 _seed_filter_widget(f"{prefix}filter_req_tags", tags, [], prefix=prefix) 

4198 host.multiselect( 

4199 "With any of these tags", 

4200 options=tags, 

4201 key=f"{prefix}filter_req_tags", 

4202 on_change=_apply, 

4203 ) 

4204 _seed_filter_widget(f"{prefix}filter_exc_tags", tags, [], prefix=prefix) 

4205 host.multiselect( 

4206 "Excluding tags", 

4207 options=tags, 

4208 key=f"{prefix}filter_exc_tags", 

4209 on_change=_apply, 

4210 help="e.g. hide everything tagged 'To exclude'.", 

4211 ) 

4212 

4213 # UX-26: the filter reset used to appear only in the empty-result diagnostic 

4214 # panel — you had to filter yourself into nothing before the escape hatch 

4215 # showed up. It now has a permanent home at the foot of the panel that set 

4216 # the filters (and a second one in the rail's Reset settings popover). 

4217 host.divider() 

4218 host.button( 

4219 "✕ Clear all filters", 

4220 key=f"{prefix}clear_all_filters_panel", 

4221 on_click=clear_trial_filters, 

4222 args=(prefix,), 

4223 width="stretch", 

4224 help="Reset every Narrow-by, condition and annotation filter.", 

4225 ) 

4226 

4227 # Mirror the rendered widget values so _seed_filter_widget can restore them on 

4228 # a run where this panel isn't shown (the keys get cleared); then publish the 

4229 # derived result for read_trial_filters (covers no-change runs). 

4230 keys = [ 

4231 f"{prefix}filter_participants", 

4232 f"{prefix}filter_text_id", 

4233 f"{prefix}filter_req_tags", 

4234 f"{prefix}filter_exc_tags", 

4235 ] + [f"{prefix}filter_{c}" for c in _filter_fields_for(words, fixations)] 

4236 st.session_state[f"{prefix}_trial_filters_raw"] = { 

4237 k: st.session_state[k] for k in keys if k in st.session_state 

4238 } 

4239 result = _compute_trial_filters(words, fixations, prefix=prefix)
